According to the officials, all government, private and civic-run schools and colleges in the city will remain closed as a precautionary measure. In a tragic incident in Mumbai's Mankhurd area, an illegal four-storey building collapsed onto a neighbouring shanty, killing 39-year-old Moinuddin Wajid Ali Shah's wife, four children and a six-year-old girl from the neighbourhood who had come over to play. “Since it had been raining heavily, I had instructed my children to stay home. I asked my wife to cook something for them and then stepped out to buy some food and household items for the family. I was barely gone for ten minutes when the incident occurred,” said Moinuddin. According to the residents, the four-storey building had started tilting, and its tiles had begun crumbling on Sunday morning. Moinuddin said that he had planned to vacate their rented home the following morning, but the structure collapsed during the mere ten minutes he stepped out to buy food. Read article Train services between Karjat and Khopoli in Raigad district partially resumed on Monday evening after remaining suspended for nearly 12 hours due to a ballast washout caused by heavy rain between Lowjee and Dolavli stations, officials said. Central Railway said the single-line track between Palasdari and Khopoli stations was declared safe after restoration work, following which the first train was allowed to pass at a speed of 10 kmph. Subsequent train movements were permitted at 30 kmph. Efforts are underway to fully restore the track between Palasdari and Khopoli stations, officials said. Chief Public Relations Officer of Central Railway Swapnil Nila had earlier said the ballast washout was reported at kilometre 109/10-11 between Lowjee and Dolavli stations, forcing the suspension of train services on the section. The Karjat-Khopoli section is part of Mumbai's suburban rail network and is used by thousands of commuters every day to travel to the metropolis for work. Suburban services on all four Central Railway corridors, namely the Main Line, Harbour Line, Trans-Harbour Line and Belapur-Uran Line were operating normally with some delays. Brief disruptions were witnessed after a plastic sheet got entangled with an overhead equipment (OHE) portal near Bhandup station on the Main Line around 1.30 pm and the branch of a tree fell near GTB station on the Harbour Line, officials said. Meanwhile, train services on the Karjat-Lonavala ghat section continue to remain suspended due to multiple landslides triggered by heavy rain, officials added. PTI Debris from the landslide on the Missing Link of the Mumbai Pune Expressway at the exit on Tunnel 2 has been cleared, MSRDC officials said. Rain-related incidents have already claimed 10 lives in Mumbai. Behind the death count are several tree-fall incidents that crushed vehicles and claimed lives. The collapse of a makeshift chawl in Mankhurd last night left six people, including five children, dead. Earlier on Sunday, a 63-year-old man died after a tree branch fell on him in Kurla. An 18-year-old boy died after a tree branch fell on him in Aarey on Saturday night. Earlier this week, an 11-year-old boy died after a tree crushed a school bus in Chembur on June 30, and a 55-year-old man died after falling into an open manhole in Sakinaka on July 2. Amid the rain fury, Maharashtra Congress president Harshvardhan Sapkal targeted the state government, alleging that the 12 rain-related deaths reported in the Mumbai region were the result of "administrative failure" and a "man-made disaster", not a natural calamity. Sapkal labelled Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis a "disaster man" rather than an "infra man", accusing the BJP-led Mahayuti government of being unprepared for the monsoon. "The 12 deaths reported in the Mumbai region amid heavy rains were the result of administrative failure and a man-made disaster, not a natural calamity," he alleged. He further criticised the Rs 7,181-crore "Missing Link", alleging that the project was marred by corruption and structural deficiencies, claiming it had to be closed just two months after its inauguration. Earlier in the day, the Pune-Mumbai Expressway had been closed between the Connecting Link and Missing Link sections after a concrete pillar fell on the carriageway amid heavy rains. Sapkal claimed that experts had raised 13 specific objections - ranging from tunnel safety to geological stability near the Lonavala dam - during the previous Congress-NCP government's tenure, but the current regime ignored these concerns to rush the project for inauguration, compromising both public safety and taxpayer funds. Labelling Fadnavis a "disaster man and not infra man", he demanded that a case of culpable homicide be registered against the chief minister. PTI Five incoming flights diverted from Mumbai to other airports till 3:30pm due to heavy rains in metropolis, officials told PTI. Another tree-falling incident has been reported in Mumbai. As rain continued to batter parts of Mumbai, a tree fell near GTB Nagar railway station on the down Harbour line towards Panvel. Suburban services on the route were disrupted for around 25 minutes, and operations resumed by 3 pm. Suburban services on the Western Railway's Vasai Road–Virar corridor remain suspended due to waterlogging at multiple railway stations. Railway officials have set up help desks at several stations, including Borivali and Virar, and are distributing food and drinking water to passengers stranded on trains. Ishika Gupta reports Between July 1 and July 5, Mumbai reported 559 tree-fall incidents, including 203 cases in the last 24 hours alone. In less than a week, three people—including an 11-year-old boy—lost their lives, while several others were injured in multiple tree-fall incidents across the city. While tree collapses are a recurring feature of the monsoon season, this year’s surge has been unprecedented, raising serious concerns over public safety. According to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s (BMC) data, 687 tree-fall incidents were reported in 2023, 653 in 2024 and 855 in 2025. The spike in such incidents has also put the spotlight on the BMC’s ambitious Rs 17,000-crore road concreting project. Notably, two of the three fatal tree-collapse incidents occurred along roads that had recently been concretised, prompting fresh questions over whether the project may have compromised the stability of roadside trees. Mumbai and its trees According to the BMC’s 2011 tree census, Mumbai had nearly 29.75 lakh trees. However, the actual number is likely to be lower today, as a significant portion of the city’s green cover has been lost over the past decade to infrastructure projects. Repeated tree collapses during successive monsoons have also contributed to the decline. Besides parks and open spaces, a large number of trees line Mumbai’s roads. Most are indigenous species such as neem, peepal, banyan and gulmohar. Many of these mature trees grow over 20 metres tall and have expansive canopies that provide much-needed shade and ecological benefits. These roadside trees are planted in square-shaped soil pits, commonly known as tree basins. However, experts have long criticised the maintenance of these basins, pointing out that many have been encroached upon by cement and concrete during road widening, road concretisation, utility trenching, fibre-optic cable laying and stormwater drain projects. Read our Explainer by Pratip Acharya Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has said that approximately 100 tonnes of debris has accumulated at the Missing Link on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway following a landslide . So far, about 70 tonnes of debris have been successfully cleared, and work to remove the remaining debris is ongoing. Right now, three lanes on the route from Mumbai towards Pune have been opened for traffic, while vehicles towards Mumbai are moving through a single lane. Public Works Minister Shivendraraje Bhosale is present at the site to oversee operations. Authorities are making efforts to restore full traffic flow within the next hour and a half. Fadnavis has appealed to citizens to avoid traveling on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway unless absolutely necessary. Visuals from Mira Road station. pic.twitter.com/N1PQu7emzT Maharashtra government on Monday directed private offices to allow employees to work from home wherever possible amid the India Meteorological Department's (IMD) red alert for Mumbai. Government and semi-government offices, except those providing essential services, will remain closed for the second half of the day. Authorities have also urged residents to avoid non-essential travel, warning that strong winds, falling trees and waterlogging could pose a serious threat to life and property. Amid heavy rainfall and a red alert in Mumbai and adjoining districts, the Bombay High Court on Monday assured that no adverse or dismissal orders would be passed in cases if lawyers were unable to reach court. Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge said the assurance would apply to all benches of the High Court in Mumbai, following requests from lawyers' associations as the India Meteorological Department warned of very heavy rain, strong winds, waterlogging and possible flash floods. (PTI) According to the new weather bulletin, IMD has issued a red alert for Mumbai, Thane, Palghar, Raigad and Ratnagiri on Monday, forecasting heavy to very heavy rain with winds of 70-80 kmph. Sindhudurg is under an orange alert. On Tuesday, Palghar and Raigad remain on red alert, while Mumbai, Thane and Ratnagiri shift to orange. Heavy monsoon rains and gusty winds disrupted flight operations at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) on Sunday, leading to four flight cancellations, around 13 diversions and over 330 delays, making it the world's most disrupted airport for the day, according to Flightradar24. Runway operations were suspended for nearly an hour due to poor visibility and strong winds reaching 42 knots before resuming after weather conditions improved. Airlines, including IndiGo and Akasa Air, also issued travel advisories, while normal flight operations resumed on Monday. Amid strong winds of 70-80 kmph and adverse weather conditions, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has issued an immediate safety advisory for all construction sites across Mumbai. Developers, contractors, architects, project managers and site engineers have been directed to secure scaffolding, cranes, tin sheets, loose materials and other temporary structures to prevent accidents. The civic body has also ordered the suspension of lifting operations and work at heights wherever weather conditions pose a risk, while mandating site-wide safety inspections, continuous weather monitoring and strict use of protective gear by workers. Stressing that the safety of workers, nearby residents and the public is paramount, the BMC warned that compliance with the advisory is mandatory until weather conditions improve. Six people, including five children, were killed after a four-storey illegal shanty collapsed onto a neighbouring structure in Mumbai's Mankhurd on Sunday night, amid heavy monsoon rains. The victims included a woman and her children, along with children from a nearby home who had come over to stay. A 24-year-old passerby was seriously injured but is now reported to be stable. Rescue teams from the fire department and the NDRF completed operations early Monday, confirming no one else was trapped. Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde said the illegally constructed building, allegedly being used as a godown, was stacked with goods that crashed onto the adjacent home when it gave way. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced an ex gratia of ₹5 lakh each for the families of those killed. article_title: Pune Rains News Live Updates: Minor landslide hits Chandanapuri Ghat, no casualties
sub_title: Mumbai-Pune Rains News Today Live Updates: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has declared a holiday for all government, private, and municipal schools and colleges in Mumbai today
article_content: Incessant rain has significantly raised the water level at Sangam, where the Mula and Mutha rivers converge, in Pune on Tuesday. Around 3.30 pm a minor landslide occurred on the Pune-bound carriageway of the Pune–Mumbai Expressway near Lonavala, resulting in rocks and debris falling onto the roadway. As a precautionary measure, traffic is being regulated through a single lane while debris clearance is being carried out by IRB. The carriageway is expected to be fully cleared and normal traffic movement restored within one hour. A minor landslide occurred on Monday afternoon on NH-60 at Chandanapuri Ghat on the Nashik to Pune carriageway. The debris was immediately cleared with the help of earthmovers, and traffic was restored without delay. There has been no loss of life or damage to property. Traffic on the highway is presently smooth and normal. Highway Police are continuously patrolling the area and monitoring the situation. Mumbai-Pune train services remained affected on Tuesday following landslides between Thakurvadi Cabin and Monkey Hill Cabin in the Lonavala-Karjat ghat section, which caused extensive damage to infrastructure. According to the latest Central Railway update, 14 trains were cancelled, five were diverted, three were short-terminated, three were short-originated, and one was rescheduled due to the disruption. Among the cancelled trains were the Pune-CSMT Deccan Express, CSMT-Pune Deccan Queen, Pune-CSMT Pragati Express, Pune-CSMT Intercity Express, Pune-CSMT Indrayani Express, CSMT-Pune Sinhagad Express, and the Pune-Solapur Intercity Express. article_content: A hydraulic crane toppled onto nearby houses in Kurla East early Friday while lifting a Poclain machine during demolition preparations, injuring 10 people, including a three-month-old baby. article_title: Pune Rains News Live Updates: Minor landslide hits Chandanapuri Ghat, no casualties
sub_title: Mumbai-Pune Rains News Today Live Updates: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has declared a holiday for all government, private, and municipal schools and colleges in Mumbai today
article_content: Incessant rain has significantly raised the water level at Sangam, where the Mula and Mutha rivers converge, in Pune on Tuesday. Around 3.30 pm a minor landslide occurred on the Pune-bound carriageway of the Pune–Mumbai Expressway near Lonavala, resulting in rocks and debris falling onto the roadway. As a precautionary measure, traffic is being regulated through a single lane while debris clearance is being carried out by IRB. The carriageway is expected to be fully cleared and normal traffic movement restored within one hour. A minor landslide occurred on Monday afternoon on NH-60 at Chandanapuri Ghat on the Nashik to Pune carriageway. The debris was immediately cleared with the help of earthmovers, and traffic was restored without delay. There has been no loss of life or damage to property. Traffic on the highway is presently smooth and normal. Highway Police are continuously patrolling the area and monitoring the situation. Mumbai-Pune train services remained affected on Tuesday following landslides between Thakurvadi Cabin and Monkey Hill Cabin in the Lonavala-Karjat ghat section, which caused extensive damage to infrastructure. According to the latest Central Railway update, 14 trains were cancelled, five were diverted, three were short-terminated, three were short-originated, and one was rescheduled due to the disruption. Among the cancelled trains were the Pune-CSMT Deccan Express, CSMT-Pune Deccan Queen, Pune-CSMT Pragati Express, Pune-CSMT Intercity Express, Pune-CSMT Indrayani Express, CSMT-Pune Sinhagad Express, and the Pune-Solapur Intercity Express. (PTI) Heavy rainfall caused the Alandi River to overflow, forcing authorities to close all four bridges to vehicular traffic as a precautionary measure. VIDEO | Pune, Maharashtra: Alandi River overflows amid heavy rainfall in the region. All four bridges closed for traffic. #punerains #punenews #monsoon (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/n147TvrpG7 ) pic.twitter.com/EbYHLOeZKG Lonavala has experienced exceptional rainfall, with the India Meteorological Department recording 670 mm in a 24-hour period, an occurrence statistically estimated to happen once every millennium. The Ghat regions of Maharashtra, which include Lonavala, remain under a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall, though conditions are anticipated to ease as the alert is downgraded to orange by Wednesday. Due to heavy rainfall and weather alerts issued by the India Meteorological Department, Pune schools remained closed on July 6 and 7, 2026, leading several institutions to implement different strategies to compensate for the lost instructional time. While schools such as The Bishop’s School, St. Mary’s School, and The Kalyani School are conducting online classes or providing home worksheets to ensure continuity, other institutions like Sanskriti School plan to make up for the missed days by utilising a compensatory Saturday. Alternatively, Jnana Prabodhini school has declared a complete holiday for students and tasked teachers with completing professional development courses via the Diksha platform, while some schools have also chosen to postpone unit tests until in-person classes resume. The Godavari River crossed the danger level in Nashik following incessant heavy rainfall on Tuesday (Jul 7), prompting authorities to remain on high alert. VIDEO | Water level crossed the danger mark in the Godavari river due to continuous heavy rainfall in Maharashtra's Nashik. Authorities on high alert. #nashik pic.twitter.com/32oy6NVCm0 The water level of the Godavari River in Nashik rose following torrential rainfall, prompting authorities to deploy security personnel at the Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga temple to ensure the safety of devotees and visitors. VIDEO | Maharashtra: Water level of Godavari River in Nashik rises following torrential rains; security personnel deployed for safety of visitors at the Triambakeshwar Jyotirling temple. (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/n147TvrpG7 ) pic.twitter.com/xpiHRElvHI Due to heavy rain and the Palkhi procession, operations at the Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) have been affected. Applicants who missed their driving test at the Institute of Driving and Traffic Research (IDTR) on July 6 have been asked to reschedule and appear for the test at their convenience within the next 10 days. Those who could not attend their learner’s licence test on Monday have been told to book a fresh appointment. Pimpri-Chinchwad RTO’s Alandi Road office will suspend vehicle inspections and driving licence testing on July 9 due to the Palkhi processions of Sant Dnyaneshwar Maharaj and Sant Tukaram Maharaj. Applicants with appointments for vehicle inspection or driving licence tests scheduled on July 9 can appear for their tests on any working day between July 10 and July 20. A day after damage to the retaining structure at the Missing Link and heavy water flow disrupted traffic on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, vehicular movement remained largely normal on Tuesday, albeit slower than usual. The Highway Police and the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) have advised motorists to avoid non-essential travel as intermittent rain continues. MSRDC and the construction company cleared the debris from the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway of the Missing Link shortly after 10 pm on Monday. Traffic was restored on two lanes after the stretch was inspected and certified safe by MSRDC, the road safety engineer and the contractor. The remaining two lanes have been kept closed due to intermittent water flow from the adjoining hillside. Over the past 48 hours, the Pune district has experienced severe weather conditions, resulting in 22 landslides, four deaths, one missing person, and over 20 injuries. District Collector Jitendra Dudi reported that extensive relief efforts, coordinated by agencies including the NDRF and local authorities, have successfully relocated over 270 citizens and rescued 30 people from a stranded bus. The heavy rainfall has caused significant infrastructure disruption, leading to the closure of nine rural roads, the Pune-Mumbai Expressway's Missing Link, and the Varandha Ghat road until August 31. While officials continue to monitor rising water levels at the Khadakwasla Dam and have temporarily restricted tourist access to forts near Lonavala, they are carefully balancing reservoir management with flood prevention measures during this El Niño year. Heavy rainfall in Pune on Monday (Jul 6), caused widespread disruption to both air and rail transport. At Pune Airport, flight operations were impacted by cancellations, diversions, and delays, prompting airlines to advise passengers to check their flight status and allow extra time for travel. Simultaneously, a major landslide in the Lonavala-Karjat section severely affected rail services, resulting in the cancellation of 26 trains, the diversion of 47 others, and various short-terminations and rescheduling, with restoration work currently underway involving hundreds of laborers. The water level of the Mula-Mutha river rises following heavy rainfall, as authorities issue a high alert over the rising water level. Due to heavy rainfall in the Khadakwasla Dam catchment area, the Pune district administration has issued an alert to residents in low-lying areas along the Mutha river, warning that water may be released from the dam's spillway at any time. With the reservoir reaching 62 percent capacity and expected to exceed 80 percent soon, authorities have advised citizens to stay out of the riverbed and relocate any vehicles or animals immediately. While recent heavy rains have significantly improved water storage levels—doubling the supply to 7 TMC from 3 TMC—civic bodies are closely monitoring the situation to determine if current water cuts in the city can be adjusted. Traffic on the Pune–Mumbai corridor of the Missing Link resumed after remaining disrupted for more than 18 hours, bringing relief to thousands of commuters stranded or affected by the prolonged closure. Authorities restored vehicular movement after ensuring the route was safe for travel following adverse weather conditions. Even as traffic has resumed, officials have urged commuters to avoid non-essential travel in view of the continuing heavy monsoon. The commuters are advised to strictly adhere to traffic advisories issued by the authorities as the rainfall may continue to impact traffic movement in the region. 🚨 IMPORTANT UPDATE ✅ Traffic has resumed on the Pune–Mumbai Connecting Link Road. Vehicular movement has been restored after completion of extensive safety operations. Despite relentless monsoon conditions, including heavy rainfall, strong winds and low visibility, MSRDC… pic.twitter.com/LCRirbWao0 The Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) on Monday evacuated residents from low-lying and riverside areas after continuous rainfall raised the risk of flooding. Residents from Ambedkar Colony, Bhatnagar and River Road were shifted to relief shelters, while evacuations were also underway in Fugewadi and Kasarwadi. Emergency teams have been deployed across the city, with JCBs, water pumps and other machinery pressed into service to tackle waterlogging in Chikhli and other affected areas. Fire department personnel also rescued a pregnant woman trapped in floodwaters at Kiwale Gaothan. PCMC Commissioner Vijay Suryavanshi urged residents to avoid unnecessary travel, stay away from rivers and flood-affected areas, and follow official advisories. Read the full report at The Indian Express here. NCP working president and Baramati MP Supriya Sule on Monday urged the Maharashtra government to allow IT employees to work from home as incessant rain disrupted normal life across Mumbai, Pune and surrounding areas. In a letter to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Sule requested that employees in establishments where remote work is feasible, including those in Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park at Hinjewadi, be allowed to work from home. Her appeal came after the Forum for IT Employees and the Pimpri Chinchwad Cooperative Housing Society Federation sought temporary WFH arrangements, citing waterlogged roads, traffic snarls and safety concerns. Sule also urged residents, particularly those living near rivers, to remain vigilant and follow official advisories. Read the full report at The Indian Express here. Barely nine weeks after its inauguration, the Rs 6,695-crore Missing Link on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway suffered its first major monsoon disruption after a landslide damaged a retaining structure near Tunnel 2, forcing the closure of the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway. While traffic on the Mumbai-to-Pune side resumed from around 10 am, Mumbai-bound vehicles continued to be diverted via the old Mumbai-Pune Highway and the ghat section as repair work and safety inspections continued. The Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) attributed the incident to exceptionally heavy rainfall, calling it an "act of God" rather than a construction flaw. Officials said the tunnel remained structurally safe, with damage confined to the retaining structure and the tunnel's external false frame. The agency said rockfall protection systems vetted by IIT Bombay remained intact and had prevented a more serious accident, while a fresh geological assessment will be carried out after the monsoon. Read the full report at The Indian Express here. Hundreds of passengers were seen waiting at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) on Monday after torrential rain severely disrupted rail connectivity, leading to the cancellation and diversion of several long-distance trains on the Central Railway mainline. (Express Photo by Ganesh Shirsekar) An two storeyed old wada Dhangar Gali in Somwar peth, located in the mid city area of Pune, collapsed amid heavy rains on Monday evening. No casualties were reported in the incident, said Pune Fire Brigade officials. An two storeyed old wada Dhangar Gali in Somwar peth, located in the mid city area of Pune, collapsed amid heavy rains on Monday evening. No casualties were reported in the incident, said Pune Fire Brigade officials | Follow Live Updates: https://t.co/87LUNIU1ll pic.twitter.com/d3RTj6KBDs The Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) has defended the newly inaugurated Mumbai-Pune Expressway Missing Link after a landslide partially shut the corridor, insisting the incident was caused by exceptionally heavy rain and not by any construction flaw. MSRDC Vice Chairman Anilkumar Gaikwad said the tunnel remained structurally safe and that only the "false frame" at the tunnel entrance was damaged after boulders rolled down from nearly 150 metres above the protected slope. Calling the incident an "act of God", officials said IIT Bombay-vetted rockfall protection systems remained intact and had prevented a more serious accident. The corporation said it would conduct a fresh geological assessment after the monsoon to examine whether additional protection measures could be installed higher up the hillside. Read the full report here at The Indian Express. The Rs 6,695-crore Mumbai-Pune Expressway Missing Link, inaugurated on May 1 as a solution to the expressway's busiest bottleneck, was partially shut on Monday after a rain-triggered landslide damaged a retaining structure near Tunnel 2. The Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway remains closed, forcing traffic onto the old Mumbai-Pune Highway, while the Mumbai-to-Pune carriageway has reopened in phases. The 13.3-km engineering project, featuring India's tallest cable-stayed bridge of its kind and one of the world's widest road tunnels, was designed to bypass the accident-prone Khandala ghat section and cut travel time by up to 30 minutes. Defending the project, the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) said the tunnel suffered no structural damage and described the landslide as an "act of God." Read the full report here at The Indian Express. Pune witnessed heavy rainfall throughout Monday, causing the water level in the Mutha river to rise significantly. The swollen river is part of the broader impact of persistent monsoon showers across the city, with authorities keeping a close watch on rivers and reservoirs. Residents have been advised to stay away from riverbanks and low-lying areas as heavy rain is expected to continue. (Express Photos By Pavan Khengre) Debris from the landslide on the Missing Link of the Mumbai-Pune Expressway at the exit on Tunnel 2 has been cleared, MSRDC officials have said. Workers while clearing the debris. (Express Photo by Narendra Vaskar) The Mutha river rose significantly on Monday following incessant rain across Pune, with people gathering on the PMC bridge near the Pune Municipal Corporation headquarters to watch the swollen river. (Express Photographs by Arul Horizon) Heavy rainfall in Pune led to a sharp rise in the Mula river's water level on Monday, with the river flowing close to the deck of Holkar Bridge in the Khadki area. The rising water levels come amid widespread rainfall across Pune district, where several rivers and reservoirs are nearing critical levels. Authorities have urged residents to remain alert and avoid venturing near swollen rivers as heavy rain is expected to continue. (Express Photographs by Arul Horizon) Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Monday reviewed the state's rain situation at the State Emergency Operation Centre (SEOC) in Mumbai, warning that the next two days would be "critical" as heavy rainfall continues across several districts. Fadnavis said rivers in Raigad, Palghar and Ratnagiri have crossed the danger mark, while rural Nashik could receive up to 350 mm of rain early Tuesday, prompting a cloudburst alert and evacuation plans. He said 500 residents in Palghar were being shifted to safer locations and instructed officials to remain on high alert for landslide-prone areas. The chief minister also appealed to warkaris not to enter Alandi for the Palkhi procession after all four bridges over the flooded Indrayani river were submerged, asking them instead to assemble in Pune. He warned of continued heavy rain, strong winds and high tide in Mumbai and the MMR, noting that 90% of the city's July rainfall had fallen in just four days, resulting in over 310 tree falls. NDRF and SDRF teams remain on standby, while citizens have been urged to avoid beaches, ghat roads and low-lying areas and strictly follow official advisories. Hundreds of passengers were seen waiting at Pune railway station on Monday after heavy rain disrupted rail services, leading to multiple train cancellations and diversions. The disruption follows heavy rainfall and a landslide that affected rail connectivity between Mumbai and Pune, forcing Central Railway to divert several long-distance trains and reschedule others. Railway authorities have urged passengers to check the latest train status before travelling. (Express photographs by Arul Horizon) Traffic continued to remain affected on the Pune-Mumbai Expressway on Monday after a landslide at the Missing Link forced the closure of both carriageways early in the morning. The Old Pune-Mumbai Highway (NH-48) was also shut after a falling tree damaged a power line, while heavy waterlogging was reported at several low-lying stretches. As of 3 pm, the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway of the Missing Link remained closed as authorities continued debris clearance and repair work. The Mumbai-to-Pune carriageway, reopened in phases from 10 am, remained affected by water flowing onto the road. The ghat section of the expressway has also been reopened and is being used to divert vehicles travelling towards Mumbai, though traffic there remains slow due to waterlogging. The Old Pune-Mumbai Highway reopened in phases from 11 am, but movement is yet to return to normal amid incessant rainfall. (Sushant Kulkarni reports for The Indian Express) Pune's Khadakwasla Dam was at 32% of its storage capacity as of 2 pm on Monday, but authorities said continued heavy rainfall and rising inflows could push the reservoir beyond 80% within the next 24 hours. The Nira Deoghar Project Division said water discharge through the dam's spillway may commence at any time depending on rainfall conditions. Residents have been advised to stay away from the riverbed, immediately move any materials or livestock from low-lying areas near the river, and remain alert to official warnings. (Soham Shah reports for The Indian Express) All four bridges over the Indrayani river have been submerged due to flooding, prompting Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis to urge warkaris to avoid the route, reported Shubhangi Khapre for The Indian Express. CM at the Maharashtra Disaster Management Control Room. Pune's Chinchwad area was inundated by 120 mm of rain between 8.30 am and 2.30 pm on Monday. In these six hours, Shivajinagar received 47 mm and Lohegaon 85 mm, with NDA recording 27.5 mm, as reported by Dipanita Nath for The Indian Express. The weather office expects the rain to continue through the day. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said around 100 tonnes of debris had accumulated after the landslide at the Missing Link on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, of which nearly 70 tonnes have been cleared so far. He said traffic from Mumbai towards Pune has resumed on three lanes, while vehicles heading towards Mumbai are moving through a single lane. Public Works Minister Shivendraraje Bhosale is overseeing the restoration work at the site, and authorities are aiming to restore full traffic movement within the next one-and-a-half hours. Fadnavis also urged commuters to avoid travelling on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway unless absolutely necessary. Central Railway has issued another update on train operations, announcing fresh diversions for several long-distance services following the landslide between Lonavala and Karjat, reported Shubham Kurale for The Indian Express. Among the affected trains are the CSMT-Chennai Egmore Express, LTT-Chennai Central Express, Konark Express, Ahmedabad-Chennai Central Express, Rajkot-Secunderabad Express, Pune-Bhuj Express, Bhubaneswar-CSMT Konark Express and Hazrat Nizamuddin-Pune Express, which have been diverted via alternate routes. Additionally, the Daund-Indore Express has been rescheduled to depart at 8.10 pm instead of its scheduled 2.10 pm departure. At 2.34 am on Monday (July 6) seven people were injured after a tree collapsed in a house at Jogeshwari. Of the total injured, four persons are currently are admitted in Cooper hospital while three persons have injured minor injuries, reported Pratip Acharya for The Indian Express. Earlier on Sunday (July 5) evening two persons were injured following a tree collapsed incident at Mumbai’s BDD Chawl at Worli. One of the injured is admitted at Nair hospital. On Sunday afternoon another 28 year old were injured after a tree collapsed on an autorickshaw. The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s (BMC) latest disaster report shows that 523 tree collapse incidents were reported in Mumbai in the last 24 hours, of which 185 were reported in the island city, 150 in the eastern suburbs and 188 in the western suburbs. Furthermore, the BMC’s data shows that one person (Yunus Kundawala - 63) lost his life, while 10 more were injured in various tree felling incidents across Mumbai,  reported Pratip Acharya for The Indian Express. The IMD has issued a red nowcast warning indicating intense spell of rainfall in Mumbai, Thane, Raigad, Nashik and Pune distritcs over next three hours, reported Pratip Acharya for The Indian Express. The weather bureau has also sounded an alarm of heavy gusty winds reaching upto 60-70 KMPH. On Monday, Shivajinagar, the main weather station of Pune, recorded 108.4 mm of rain in 24 hours till 8.30 am. This is the highest rainfall received in Shivajinagar in the month of July, since 114.1 mm was recorded on July 25, 2024. Pune has received more rain only two times before since records started in 1896;117.9 mm on July 27, 1967, and 130.4 mm on July 19, 1958. Two people have died, and two more from the same family are feared trapped after a landslide on a house in Patan village near Lohagad Fort in Maval taluka of Pune district in the early hours of Monday. A team from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), which had been deployed in response, has recovered two bodies. "A landslide struck a house in Patan village of Maval taluka in the early hours of Monday. According to preliminary information, there is a possibility that the entire family of four people residing in the house is trapped under the debris," said an officer. "Till now two bodies have been recovered and search and rescue efforts are currently on," the officer added. A total of 24 persons, including 20 police personnel of the Navi Mumbai Police Force and 4 other citizens, trapped in the Bhakta Niwas building in Alandi since 6 am today,  were rescued safely. article_content: Maharashtra Chief Minister's Office (CMO) on Tuesday asked farmers to plan agricultural activities in accordance with the weather situation as a significant decrease in rainfall is expected in parts of the state from July 8. While parts of Maharashtra faced heavy rainfall, the state's Agriculture Department urged the farmers in areas with less than satisfactory rainfall not to rush into sowing until sufficient moisture is created in the soil. In a statement on X, the CMO stated, "Although there was heavy rainfall in Mumbai and Western Maharashtra at the beginning of July, rainfall across various parts of the state so far has been below average. Particularly, the amount of rainfall is low in Khandesh (Dhule and Nandurbar), Central Maharashtra (Ahilyanagar and Solapur), parts of Western Vidarbha, and some areas of Marathwada." ANI A hearing on a plea by the Mumbai civic body turned into a blunt assessment of the civic sense of citizens on Tuesday, with the Bombay High Court flagging the people's "uncanny knack" for land grab and dumping of waste in drains, which it said causes water-logging in monsoon. Our habit is to rob our own motherland, the High Court said as it pointed to encroachment of footpaths, rendering them inaccessible for pedestrians. Citizens should stop blaming the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) alone for monsoon water-logging, a bench of acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad said, noting that encroachments and clogged drains are "our own creation" and flooding is obvious during monsoon. "We have an uncanny knack for grabbing lands. We put all the dirt and material inside, and we block the gutters. One small spell of rain blocks the roads in Mumbai. It's our own creation," the bench said. PTI El Nino, the recurrent weather pattern that drives up global temperatures, and climate change cannot be viewed independently as one is delaying the rains and the other intensifying them, according to climate experts. A rapidly strengthening El Nino in the Pacific delayed the onset of the monsoon and kept rainfall subdued through June, leaving India with a 40 per cent rainfall deficit by the end of the month. Yet, within days, the scenario changed dramatically. As the monsoon entered an active phase by the end of June, Mumbai and large parts of India's West Coast were battered by exceptionally intense rainfall. Experts say the new reality that climate change is fundamentally altering the behaviour of the Indian monsoon. "Monsoon is presently in an active phase, with several weather systems prevailing across the country. There was a depression over Odisha and a cyclonic circulation over Maharashtra, keeping the western and eastern arms of monsoon active," said Mahesh Palawat, Vice President - Meteorology and Climate Change, Skymet Weather. "Along with this, continuous moisture feed from the Arabian Sea led to continuous regeneration of clouds over Maharashtra in the last three-four days, leading to heavy rainfall," Palawat said. Raghu Murtugudde, Emeritus Professor, University of Maryland and retired professor, IIT-Mumbai, explained that Mumbai saw delayed onset of monsoon which is partly explainable by El Nino. PTI The sowing area across eight districts of the Marathwada region in Maharashtra shrank by 17.87 lakh hectares compared to the corresponding period last year due to the delayed onset of monsoon, officials said on Tuesday. The overall sowing percentage in the region comprising Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Jalna, Beed, Parbhani, Nanded, Hingoli, Dharashiv and Latur districts is around 58 per cent. The average land under cultivation in the last five years was 49.72 lakh hectares. In 2025, sowing took place on 42.42 lakh hectares. However, the area under cultivation shrank to 24.55 lakh hectares as of now, according to a report from the agriculture department. Suburban services on all four Central Railway corridors, namely the Main Line, Harbour Line, Trans-Harbour Line and Belapur-Uran Line were operating normally with some delays. PTI Debris from the landslide on the Missing Link of the Mumbai Pune Expressway at the exit on Tunnel 2 has been cleared, MSRDC officials said. Rain-related incidents have already claimed 10 lives in Mumbai. Behind the death count are several tree-fall incidents that crushed vehicles and claimed lives. The collapse of a makeshift chawl in Mankhurd last night left six people, including five children, dead. Earlier on Sunday, a 63-year-old man died after a tree branch fell on him in Kurla. An 18-year-old boy died after a tree branch fell on him in Aarey on Saturday night. Earlier this week, an 11-year-old boy died after a tree crushed a school bus in Chembur on June 30, and a 55-year-old man died after falling into an open manhole in Sakinaka on July 2. Amid the rain fury, Maharashtra Congress president Harshvardhan Sapkal targeted the state government, alleging that the 12 rain-related deaths reported in the Mumbai region were the result of "administrative failure" and a "man-made disaster", not a natural calamity. Sapkal labelled Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis a "disaster man" rather than an "infra man", accusing the BJP-led Mahayuti government of being unprepared for the monsoon. "The 12 deaths reported in the Mumbai region amid heavy rains were the result of administrative failure and a man-made disaster, not a natural calamity," he alleged. He further criticised the Rs 7,181-crore "Missing Link", alleging that the project was marred by corruption and structural deficiencies, claiming it had to be closed just two months after its inauguration. Earlier in the day, the Pune-Mumbai Expressway had been closed between the Connecting Link and Missing Link sections after a concrete pillar fell on the carriageway amid heavy rains. Sapkal claimed that experts had raised 13 specific objections - ranging from tunnel safety to geological stability near the Lonavala dam - during the previous Congress-NCP government's tenure, but the current regime ignored these concerns to rush the project for inauguration, compromising both public safety and taxpayer funds. Labelling Fadnavis a "disaster man and not infra man", he demanded that a case of culpable homicide be registered against the chief minister. Ishika Gupta reports Between July 1 and July 5, Mumbai reported 559 tree-fall incidents, including 203 cases in the last 24 hours alone. In less than a week, three people—including an 11-year-old boy—lost their lives, while several others were injured in multiple tree-fall incidents across the city. While tree collapses are a recurring feature of the monsoon season, this year’s surge has been unprecedented, raising serious concerns over public safety. According to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s (BMC) data, 687 tree-fall incidents were reported in 2023, 653 in 2024 and 855 in 2025. The spike in such incidents has also put the spotlight on the BMC’s ambitious Rs 17,000-crore road concreting project. Notably, two of the three fatal tree-collapse incidents occurred along roads that had recently been concretised, prompting fresh questions over whether the project may have compromised the stability of roadside trees. Mumbai and its trees According to the BMC’s 2011 tree census, Mumbai had nearly 29.75 lakh trees. However, the actual number is likely to be lower today, as a significant portion of the city’s green cover has been lost over the past decade to infrastructure projects. Repeated tree collapses during successive monsoons have also contributed to the decline. Besides parks and open spaces, a large number of trees line Mumbai’s roads. Most are indigenous species such as neem, peepal, banyan and gulmohar. Many of these mature trees grow over 20 metres tall and have expansive canopies that provide much-needed shade and ecological benefits. These roadside trees are planted in square-shaped soil pits, commonly known as tree basins. However, experts have long criticised the maintenance of these basins, pointing out that many have been encroached upon by cement and concrete during road widening, road concretisation, utility trenching, fibre-optic cable laying and stormwater drain projects. Professional Background

Role: Correspondent coverig education and city affairs in Pune.

Specialization: His primary beat is education, but he also maintains a strong focus on civic issues, public health, human rights, and state politics.

Key Strength: Soham focuses on data-driven reporting on school and college education, government reports, and public infrastructure.

Recent Notable Articles (Late 2025)

His late 2025 work highlights a transition from education-centric reporting to hard-hitting investigative and human-rights stories:

Signature Style

Soham is known for his civil-liberties lens. She notes that there is no fixed timeline for grief and that people can maintain “continuing bonds” through memories, values, traditions, stories and the influence of those they have lost. Her advice is to appreciate loved ones while they are present—ask about their lives and dreams, record their voices, preserve family traditions, take photographs and express gratitude and love—because the moments we consider ordinary may eventually become the ones we cherish most.

article_title: Pune Rains News Live Updates: Minor landslide hits Chandanapuri Ghat, no casualties
sub_title: Mumbai-Pune Rains News Today Live Updates: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has declared a holiday for all government, private, and municipal schools and colleges in Mumbai today
article_content: Incessant rain has significantly raised the water level at Sangam, where the Mula and Mutha rivers converge, in Pune on Tuesday. Around 3.30 pm a minor landslide occurred on the Pune-bound carriageway of the Pune–Mumbai Expressway near Lonavala, resulting in rocks and debris falling onto the roadway. As a precautionary measure, traffic is being regulated through a single lane while debris clearance is being carried out by IRB. The carriageway is expected to be fully cleared and normal traffic movement restored within one hour. A minor landslide occurred on Monday afternoon on NH-60 at Chandanapuri Ghat on the Nashik to Pune carriageway. The debris was immediately cleared with the help of earthmovers, and traffic was restored without delay. There has been no loss of life or damage to property. Traffic on the highway is presently smooth and normal. Highway Police are continuously patrolling the area and monitoring the situation. Mumbai-Pune train services remained affected on Tuesday following landslides between Thakurvadi Cabin and Monkey Hill Cabin in the Lonavala-Karjat ghat section, which caused extensive damage to infrastructure. According to the latest Central Railway update, 14 trains were cancelled, five were diverted, three were short-terminated, three were short-originated, and one was rescheduled due to the disruption. Among the cancelled trains were the Pune-CSMT Deccan Express, CSMT-Pune Deccan Queen, Pune-CSMT Pragati Express, Pune-CSMT Intercity Express, Pune-CSMT Indrayani Express, CSMT-Pune Sinhagad Express, and the Pune-Solapur Intercity Express. (PTI) Heavy rainfall caused the Alandi River to overflow, forcing authorities to close all four bridges to vehicular traffic as a precautionary measure. The Ghat regions of Maharashtra, which include Lonavala, remain under a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall, though conditions are anticipated to ease as the alert is downgraded to orange by Wednesday. Due to heavy rainfall and weather alerts issued by the India Meteorological Department, Pune schools remained closed on July 6 and 7, 2026, leading several institutions to implement different strategies to compensate for the lost instructional time. While schools such as The Bishop’s School, St. Mary’s School, and The Kalyani School are conducting online classes or providing home worksheets to ensure continuity, other institutions like Sanskriti School plan to make up for the missed days by utilising a compensatory Saturday. Alternatively, Jnana Prabodhini school has declared a complete holiday for students and tasked teachers with completing professional development courses via the Diksha platform, while some schools have also chosen to postpone unit tests until in-person classes resume. Applicants who missed their driving test at the Institute of Driving and Traffic Research (IDTR) on July 6 have been asked to reschedule and appear for the test at their convenience within the next 10 days. Those who could not attend their learner’s licence test on Monday have been told to book a fresh appointment. Pimpri-Chinchwad RTO’s Alandi Road office will suspend vehicle inspections and driving licence testing on July 9 due to the Palkhi processions of Sant Dnyaneshwar Maharaj and Sant Tukaram Maharaj. Applicants with appointments for vehicle inspection or driving licence tests scheduled on July 9 can appear for their tests on any working day between July 10 and July 20. A day after damage to the retaining structure at the Missing Link and heavy water flow disrupted traffic on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, vehicular movement remained largely normal on Tuesday, albeit slower than usual. The Highway Police and the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) have advised motorists to avoid non-essential travel as intermittent rain continues. MSRDC and the construction company cleared the debris from the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway of the Missing Link shortly after 10 pm on Monday. Traffic was restored on two lanes after the stretch was inspected and certified safe by MSRDC, the road safety engineer and the contractor. The remaining two lanes have been kept closed due to intermittent water flow from the adjoining hillside. Over the past 48 hours, the Pune district has experienced severe weather conditions, resulting in 22 landslides, four deaths, one missing person, and over 20 injuries. District Collector Jitendra Dudi reported that extensive relief efforts, coordinated by agencies including the NDRF and local authorities, have successfully relocated over 270 citizens and rescued 30 people from a stranded bus. The heavy rainfall has caused significant infrastructure disruption, leading to the closure of nine rural roads, the Pune-Mumbai Expressway's Missing Link, and the Varandha Ghat road until August 31. While officials continue to monitor rising water levels at the Khadakwasla Dam and have temporarily restricted tourist access to forts near Lonavala, they are carefully balancing reservoir management with flood prevention measures during this El Niño year. Heavy rainfall in Pune on Monday (Jul 6), caused widespread disruption to both air and rail transport. At Pune Airport, flight operations were impacted by cancellations, diversions, and delays, prompting airlines to advise passengers to check their flight status and allow extra time for travel. Simultaneously, a major landslide in the Lonavala-Karjat section severely affected rail services, resulting in the cancellation of 26 trains, the diversion of 47 others, and various short-terminations and rescheduling, with restoration work currently underway involving hundreds of laborers. The water level of the Mula-Mutha river rises following heavy rainfall, as authorities issue a high alert over the rising water level. Due to heavy rainfall in the Khadakwasla Dam catchment area, the Pune district administration has issued an alert to residents in low-lying areas along the Mutha river, warning that water may be released from the dam's spillway at any time. With the reservoir reaching 62 percent capacity and expected to exceed 80 percent soon, authorities have advised citizens to stay out of the riverbed and relocate any vehicles or animals immediately. While recent heavy rains have significantly improved water storage levels—doubling the supply to 7 TMC from 3 TMC—civic bodies are closely monitoring the situation to determine if current water cuts in the city can be adjusted. Traffic on the Pune–Mumbai corridor of the Missing Link resumed after remaining disrupted for more than 18 hours, bringing relief to thousands of commuters stranded or affected by the prolonged closure. Authorities restored vehicular movement after ensuring the route was safe for travel following adverse weather conditions. Even as traffic has resumed, officials have urged commuters to avoid non-essential travel in view of the continuing heavy monsoon. The commuters are advised to strictly adhere to traffic advisories issued by the authorities as the rainfall may continue to impact traffic movement in the region. 🚨 IMPORTANT UPDATE ✅ Traffic has resumed on the Pune–Mumbai Connecting Link Road. Residents from Ambedkar Colony, Bhatnagar and River Road were shifted to relief shelters, while evacuations were also underway in Fugewadi and Kasarwadi. Emergency teams have been deployed across the city, with JCBs, water pumps and other machinery pressed into service to tackle waterlogging in Chikhli and other affected areas. Fire department personnel also rescued a pregnant woman trapped in floodwaters at Kiwale Gaothan. PCMC Commissioner Vijay Suryavanshi urged residents to avoid unnecessary travel, stay away from rivers and flood-affected areas, and follow official advisories. In a letter to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Sule requested that employees in establishments where remote work is feasible, including those in Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park at Hinjewadi, be allowed to work from home. Barely nine weeks after its inauguration, the Rs 6,695-crore Missing Link on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway suffered its first major monsoon disruption after a landslide damaged a retaining structure near Tunnel 2, forcing the closure of the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway. While traffic on the Mumbai-to-Pune side resumed from around 10 am, Mumbai-bound vehicles continued to be diverted via the old Mumbai-Pune Highway and the ghat section as repair work and safety inspections continued. The Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) attributed the incident to exceptionally heavy rainfall, calling it an "act of God" rather than a construction flaw. Officials said the tunnel remained structurally safe, with damage confined to the retaining structure and the tunnel's external false frame. The agency said rockfall protection systems vetted by IIT Bombay remained intact and had prevented a more serious accident, while a fresh geological assessment will be carried out after the monsoon. MSRDC Vice Chairman Anilkumar Gaikwad said the tunnel remained structurally safe and that only the "false frame" at the tunnel entrance was damaged after boulders rolled down from nearly 150 metres above the protected slope. Calling the incident an "act of God", officials said IIT Bombay-vetted rockfall protection systems remained intact and had prevented a more serious accident. The Rs 6,695-crore Mumbai-Pune Expressway Missing Link, inaugurated on May 1 as a solution to the expressway's busiest bottleneck, was partially shut on Monday after a rain-triggered landslide damaged a retaining structure near Tunnel 2. The Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway remains closed, forcing traffic onto the old Mumbai-Pune Highway, while the Mumbai-to-Pune carriageway has reopened in phases. The 13.3-km engineering project, featuring India's tallest cable-stayed bridge of its kind and one of the world's widest road tunnels, was designed to bypass the accident-prone Khandala ghat section and cut travel time by up to 30 minutes. Defending the project, the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) said the tunnel suffered no structural damage and described the landslide as an "act of God." Read the full report here at The Indian Express. Pune witnessed heavy rainfall throughout Monday, causing the water level in the Mutha river to rise significantly. The swollen river is part of the broader impact of persistent monsoon showers across the city, with authorities keeping a close watch on rivers and reservoirs. Residents have been advised to stay away from riverbanks and low-lying areas as heavy rain is expected to continue. He said 500 residents in Palghar were being shifted to safer locations and instructed officials to remain on high alert for landslide-prone areas. The chief minister also appealed to warkaris not to enter Alandi for the Palkhi procession after all four bridges over the flooded Indrayani river were submerged, asking them instead to assemble in Pune. He warned of continued heavy rain, strong winds and high tide in Mumbai and the MMR, noting that 90% of the city's July rainfall had fallen in just four days, resulting in over 310 tree falls. NDRF and SDRF teams remain on standby, while citizens have been urged to avoid beaches, ghat roads and low-lying areas and strictly follow official advisories. Hundreds of passengers were seen waiting at Pune railway station on Monday after heavy rain disrupted rail services, leading to multiple train cancellations and diversions. The disruption follows heavy rainfall and a landslide that affected rail connectivity between Mumbai and Pune, forcing Central Railway to divert several long-distance trains and reschedule others. Railway authorities have urged passengers to check the latest train status before travelling. (Express photographs by Arul Horizon) Traffic continued to remain affected on the Pune-Mumbai Expressway on Monday after a landslide at the Missing Link forced the closure of both carriageways early in the morning. As of 3 pm, the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway of the Missing Link remained closed as authorities continued debris clearance and repair work. The Mumbai-to-Pune carriageway, reopened in phases from 10 am, remained affected by water flowing onto the road. The ghat section of the expressway has also been reopened and is being used to divert vehicles travelling towards Mumbai, though traffic there remains slow due to waterlogging. The Old Pune-Mumbai Highway reopened in phases from 11 am, but movement is yet to return to normal amid incessant rainfall. (Sushant Kulkarni reports for The Indian Express) Pune's Khadakwasla Dam was at 32% of its storage capacity as of 2 pm on Monday, but authorities said continued heavy rainfall and rising inflows could push the reservoir beyond 80% within the next 24 hours. The Nira Deoghar Project Division said water discharge through the dam's spillway may commence at any time depending on rainfall conditions. Residents have been advised to stay away from the riverbed, immediately move any materials or livestock from low-lying areas near the river, and remain alert to official warnings. The weather office expects the rain to continue through the day. He said traffic from Mumbai towards Pune has resumed on three lanes, while vehicles heading towards Mumbai are moving through a single lane. Public Works Minister Shivendraraje Bhosale is overseeing the restoration work at the site, and authorities are aiming to restore full traffic movement within the next one-and-a-half hours. Fadnavis also urged commuters to avoid travelling on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway unless absolutely necessary. Among the affected trains are the CSMT-Chennai Egmore Express, LTT-Chennai Central Express, Konark Express, Ahmedabad-Chennai Central Express, Rajkot-Secunderabad Express, Pune-Bhuj Express, Bhubaneswar-CSMT Konark Express and Hazrat Nizamuddin-Pune Express, which have been diverted via alternate routes. The IMD has issued a red nowcast warning indicating intense spell of rainfall in Mumbai, Thane, Raigad, Nashik and Pune distritcs over next three hours, reported Pratip Acharya for The Indian Express. The weather bureau has also sounded an alarm of heavy gusty winds reaching upto 60-70 KMPH. This is the highest rainfall received in Shivajinagar in the month of July, since 114.1 mm was recorded on July 25, 2024. Pune has received more rain only two times before since records started in 1896;117.9 mm on July 27, 1967, and 130.4 mm on July 19, 1958. article_content: Maharashtra Chief Minister's Office (CMO) on Tuesday asked farmers to plan agricultural activities in accordance with the weather situation as a significant decrease in rainfall is expected in parts of the state from July 8. While parts of Maharashtra faced heavy rainfall, the state's Agriculture Department urged the farmers in areas with less than satisfactory rainfall not to rush into sowing until sufficient moisture is created in the soil. In a statement on X, the CMO stated, "Although there was heavy rainfall in Mumbai and Western Maharashtra at the beginning of July, rainfall across various parts of the state so far has been below average. Particularly, the amount of rainfall is low in Khandesh (Dhule and Nandurbar), Central Maharashtra (Ahilyanagar and Solapur), parts of Western Vidarbha, and some areas of Marathwada." ANI A hearing on a plea by the Mumbai civic body turned into a blunt assessment of the civic sense of citizens on Tuesday, with the Bombay High Court flagging the people's "uncanny knack" for land grab and dumping of waste in drains, which it said causes water-logging in monsoon. Our habit is to rob our own motherland, the High Court said as it pointed to encroachment of footpaths, rendering them inaccessible for pedestrians. Citizens should stop blaming the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) alone for monsoon water-logging, a bench of acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad said, noting that encroachments and clogged drains are "our own creation" and flooding is obvious during monsoon. "We have an uncanny knack for grabbing lands. We put all the dirt and material inside, and we block the gutters. One small spell of rain blocks the roads in Mumbai. It's our own creation," the bench said. PTI El Nino, the recurrent weather pattern that drives up global temperatures, and climate change cannot be viewed independently as one is delaying the rains and the other intensifying them, according to climate experts. A rapidly strengthening El Nino in the Pacific delayed the onset of the monsoon and kept rainfall subdued through June, leaving India with a 40 per cent rainfall deficit by the end of the month. Yet, within days, the scenario changed dramatically. As the monsoon entered an active phase by the end of June, Mumbai and large parts of India's West Coast were battered by exceptionally intense rainfall. Experts say the new reality that climate change is fundamentally altering the behaviour of the Indian monsoon. "Monsoon is presently in an active phase, with several weather systems prevailing across the country. There was a depression over Odisha and a cyclonic circulation over Maharashtra, keeping the western and eastern arms of monsoon active," said Mahesh Palawat, Vice President - Meteorology and Climate Change, Skymet Weather. "Along with this, continuous moisture feed from the Arabian Sea led to continuous regeneration of clouds over Maharashtra in the last three-four days, leading to heavy rainfall," Palawat said. Raghu Murtugudde, Emeritus Professor, University of Maryland and retired professor, IIT-Mumbai, explained that Mumbai saw delayed onset of monsoon which is partly explainable by El Nino. PTI The sowing area across eight districts of the Marathwada region in Maharashtra shrank by 17.87 lakh hectares compared to the corresponding period last year due to the delayed onset of monsoon, officials said on Tuesday. The overall sowing percentage in the region comprising Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Jalna, Beed, Parbhani, Nanded, Hingoli, Dharashiv and Latur districts is around 58 per cent. The average land under cultivation in the last five years was 49.72 lakh hectares. In 2025, sowing took place on 42.42 lakh hectares. However, the area under cultivation shrank to 24.55 lakh hectares as of now, according to a report from the agriculture department. PTI Around 3.30 pm a minor landslide occurred on the Pune-bound carriageway of the Pune–Mumbai Expressway near Lonavala, resulting in rocks and debris falling onto the roadway. As a precautionary measure, traffic is being regulated through a single lane while debris clearance is being carried out by IRB. The carriageway is expected to be fully cleared and normal traffic movement restored within one hour. Two minor boys drowned, while two women suffered injuries as cement sheets collapsed at a garden in Mumbai during heavy rains and winds during the last 24 hours, officials said on Tuesday. The two boys, aged 17 and 14, drowned in flood waters in Malad and Govandi areas on Monday evening. Meanwhile, the two women were injured after cement sheets from an adjoining structure collapsed while they were practising yoga at a private garden in the Lokhandwala area in Andheri. They were admitted to the hospital and reported to be in stable condition, the BMC said. Waterlogging in Virar has largely subsided, though a few pockets remain flooded following Monday's heavy showers. (Express Photos by Akash Patil) s Bombay High Court recently observed that Mumbai's frequent flooding is a man-made issue caused by illegal land grabbing, the obstruction of drainage systems, and the unauthorized use of footpaths for commercial and parking purposes, rather than being solely the fault of the Municipal Corporation. During a hearing regarding road widening in Mandala village, the court criticized the public for ignoring legal standards until facing demolition notices, while also addressing the ongoing dispute over expanding a road near the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre. The BMC reported that while they have cleared encroachments for a 30-foot road, further widening to 50 feet requires the cooperation of the Union Department of Atomic Energy, which the court has now formally notified to provide a decision. Lonavala has experienced exceptional rainfall, with the India Meteorological Department recording 670 mm in a 24-hour period, an occurrence statistically estimated to happen once every millennium. The Ghat regions of Maharashtra, which include Lonavala, remain under a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall, though conditions are anticipated to ease as the alert is downgraded to orange by Wednesday. The members of Opposition, on Tuesday, demanded a discussion on the rain situation in the Maharashtra assembly, citing widespread damage and a rising death toll. Speaker Rahul Narwekar said that the adjournment notices moved by the Opposition did not meet the rules and were not admitted. However, he asked the Opposition to raise the issue via a half-an-hour discussion. Representatives from the Congress, NCP (SP), and Shiv Sena (UBT) highlighted severe disruptions in both urban and rural areas. Jayant Patil of NCP (SP) said that 12 people were killed in rain-related incidents over the last two to three days. Alleging administrative lapses, he emphasised that the Opposition wanted the government to respond to the situation. Heavy rainfall continued to lash parts of Thane city on Tuesday (Jul 7), with visuals from the Rabodi area showing intense showers as monsoon activity remained vigorous across Maharashtra. Rescue teams are on the scene after one person was rescued, while efforts continue to reach those still trapped. The building collapse in Mumbai’s Mankhurd that claimed six lives, including five minors, has once again turned the spotlight on the area’s long-standing problem of illegal and structurally unsafe housing. The Mankhurd-Shivaji Nagar belt is dotted with informal settlements, ageing chawls and unauthorised multi-storey structures, many built on low-lying land prone to flooding and prolonged waterlogging during the monsoon. Weak soil conditions, ageing buildings and rampant unauthorised construction have made these neighbourhoods among the most vulnerable in Mumbai to monsoon-related collapses. In a tragic incident in Mumbai's Mankhurd area, an illegal four-storey building collapsed onto a neighbouring shanty, killing 39-year-old Moinuddin Wajid Ali Shah's wife, four children and a six-year-old girl from the neighbourhood who had come over to play. “Since it had been raining heavily, I had instructed my children to stay home. I asked my wife to cook something for them and then stepped out to buy some food and household items for the family. I was barely gone for ten minutes when the incident occurred,” said Moinuddin. According to the residents, the four-storey building had started tilting, and its tiles had begun crumbling on Sunday morning. Moinuddin said that he had planned to vacate their rented home the following morning, but the structure collapsed during the mere ten minutes he stepped out to buy food. Read article Train services between Karjat and Khopoli in Raigad district partially resumed on Monday evening after remaining suspended for nearly 12 hours due to a ballast washout caused by heavy rain between Lowjee and Dolavli stations, officials said. Central Railway said the single-line track between Palasdari and Khopoli stations was declared safe after restoration work, following which the first train was allowed to pass at a speed of 10 kmph. Subsequent train movements were permitted at 30 kmph. Efforts are underway to fully restore the track between Palasdari and Khopoli stations, officials said. Chief Public Relations Officer of Central Railway Swapnil Nila had earlier said the ballast washout was reported at kilometre 109/10-11 between Lowjee and Dolavli stations, forcing the suspension of train services on the section. The Karjat-Khopoli section is part of Mumbai's suburban rail network and is used by thousands of commuters every day to travel to the metropolis for work. Suburban services on all four Central Railway corridors, namely the Main Line, Harbour Line, Trans-Harbour Line and Belapur-Uran Line were operating normally with some delays. Brief disruptions were witnessed after a plastic sheet got entangled with an overhead equipment (OHE) portal near Bhandup station on the Main Line around 1.30 pm and the branch of a tree fell near GTB station on the Harbour Line, officials said. Meanwhile, train services on the Karjat-Lonavala ghat section continue to remain suspended due to multiple landslides triggered by heavy rain, officials added. PTI Debris from the landslide on the Missing Link of the Mumbai Pune Expressway at the exit on Tunnel 2 has been cleared, MSRDC officials said. Rain-related incidents have already claimed 10 lives in Mumbai. Behind the death count are several tree-fall incidents that crushed vehicles and claimed lives. The collapse of a makeshift chawl in Mankhurd last night left six people, including five children, dead. Earlier on Sunday, a 63-year-old man died after a tree branch fell on him in Kurla. An 18-year-old boy died after a tree branch fell on him in Aarey on Saturday night. Earlier this week, an 11-year-old boy died after a tree crushed a school bus in Chembur on June 30, and a 55-year-old man died after falling into an open manhole in Sakinaka on July 2. Amid the rain fury, Maharashtra Congress president Harshvardhan Sapkal targeted the state government, alleging that the 12 rain-related deaths reported in the Mumbai region were the result of "administrative failure" and a "man-made disaster", not a natural calamity. Sapkal labelled Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis a "disaster man" rather than an "infra man", accusing the BJP-led Mahayuti government of being unprepared for the monsoon. "The 12 deaths reported in the Mumbai region amid heavy rains were the result of administrative failure and a man-made disaster, not a natural calamity," he alleged. He further criticised the Rs 7,181-crore "Missing Link", alleging that the project was marred by corruption and structural deficiencies, claiming it had to be closed just two months after its inauguration. Earlier in the day, the Pune-Mumbai Expressway had been closed between the Connecting Link and Missing Link sections after a concrete pillar fell on the carriageway amid heavy rains. Sapkal claimed that experts had raised 13 specific objections - ranging from tunnel safety to geological stability near the Lonavala dam - during the previous Congress-NCP government's tenure, but the current regime ignored these concerns to rush the project for inauguration, compromising both public safety and taxpayer funds. Labelling Fadnavis a "disaster man and not infra man", he demanded that a case of culpable homicide be registered against the chief minister. PTI Five incoming flights diverted from Mumbai to other airports till 3:30pm due to heavy rains in metropolis, officials told PTI. Another tree-falling incident has been reported in Mumbai. As rain continued to batter parts of Mumbai, a tree fell near GTB Nagar railway station on the down Harbour line towards Panvel. Suburban services on the route were disrupted for around 25 minutes, and operations resumed by 3 pm. Suburban services on the Western Railway's Vasai Road–Virar corridor remain suspended due to waterlogging at multiple railway stations. Railway officials have set up help desks at several stations, including Borivali and Virar, and are distributing food and drinking water to passengers stranded on trains. Ishika Gupta reports Between July 1 and July 5, Mumbai reported 559 tree-fall incidents, including 203 cases in the last 24 hours alone. In less than a week, three people—including an 11-year-old boy—lost their lives, while several others were injured in multiple tree-fall incidents across the city. While tree collapses are a recurring feature of the monsoon season, this year’s surge has been unprecedented, raising serious concerns over public safety. According to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s (BMC) data, 687 tree-fall incidents were reported in 2023, 653 in 2024 and 855 in 2025. The spike in such incidents has also put the spotlight on the BMC’s ambitious Rs 17,000-crore road concreting project. Notably, two of the three fatal tree-collapse incidents occurred along roads that had recently been concretised, prompting fresh questions over whether the project may have compromised the stability of roadside trees. Mumbai and its trees According to the BMC’s 2011 tree census, Mumbai had nearly 29.75 lakh trees. However, the actual number is likely to be lower today, as a significant portion of the city’s green cover has been lost over the past decade to infrastructure projects. Repeated tree collapses during successive monsoons have also contributed to the decline. Besides parks and open spaces, a large number of trees line Mumbai’s roads. Most are indigenous species such as neem, peepal, banyan and gulmohar. Many of these mature trees grow over 20 metres tall and have expansive canopies that provide much-needed shade and ecological benefits. These roadside trees are planted in square-shaped soil pits, commonly known as tree basins. However, experts have long criticised the maintenance of these basins, pointing out that many have been encroached upon by cement and concrete during road widening, road concretisation, utility trenching, fibre-optic cable laying and stormwater drain projects. So far, about 70 tonnes of debris have been successfully cleared, and work to remove the remaining debris is ongoing. Right now, three lanes on the route from Mumbai towards Pune have been opened for traffic, while vehicles towards Mumbai are moving through a single lane. Public Works Minister Shivendraraje Bhosale is present at the site to oversee operations. Authorities are making efforts to restore full traffic flow within the next hour and a half. Authorities have also urged residents to avoid non-essential travel, warning that strong winds, falling trees and waterlogging could pose a serious threat to life and property. Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge said the assurance would apply to all benches of the High Court in Mumbai, following requests from lawyers' associations as the India Meteorological Department warned of very heavy rain, strong winds, waterlogging and possible flash floods. (PTI) According to the new weather bulletin, IMD has issued a red alert for Mumbai, Thane, Palghar, Raigad and Ratnagiri on Monday, forecasting heavy to very heavy rain with winds of 70-80 kmph. Heavy monsoon rains and gusty winds disrupted flight operations at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) on Sunday, leading to four flight cancellations, around 13 diversions and over 330 delays, making it the world's most disrupted airport for the day, according to Flightradar24. Runway operations were suspended for nearly an hour due to poor visibility and strong winds reaching 42 knots before resuming after weather conditions improved. Airlines, including IndiGo and Akasa Air, also issued travel advisories, while normal flight operations resumed on Monday. Amid strong winds of 70-80 kmph and adverse weather conditions, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has issued an immediate safety advisory for all construction sites across Mumbai. Developers, contractors, architects, project managers and site engineers have been directed to secure scaffolding, cranes, tin sheets, loose materials and other temporary structures to prevent accidents. The civic body has also ordered the suspension of lifting operations and work at heights wherever weather conditions pose a risk, while mandating site-wide safety inspections, continuous weather monitoring and strict use of protective gear by workers. Stressing that the safety of workers, nearby residents and the public is paramount, the BMC warned that compliance with the advisory is mandatory until weather conditions improve.
