Psychotherapist Delnna Rrajesh explains that ordinary memories, familiar habits and everyday moments can become especially precious after a loss, while grief can also include mourning milestones and experiences a loved one never got to witness. She notes that there is no fixed timeline for grief and that people can maintain “continuing bonds” through memories, values, traditions, stories and the influence of those they have lost. Her advice is to appreciate loved ones while they are present—ask about their lives and dreams, record their voices, preserve family traditions, take photographs and express gratitude and love—because the moments we consider ordinary may eventually become the ones we cherish most.

sub_title: Great Khali, 53, recently shared a video of himself performing knuckle (fist) push-ups, prompting experts to explain the benefits of this advanced exercise. According to orthopaedic specialist Dr Mrinal Prakash, knuckle push-ups help build upper-body strength, improve wrist and forearm stability, grip strength, muscular endurance, and body control because the exercise is performed on a much smaller base of support than regular push-ups. While Khali’s ability to perform them demonstrates impressive strength, coordination, and control, the exercise is significantly more demanding on the knuckles, wrists, shoulders, and core. Beginners should not start with knuckle push-ups; instead, they should first develop proper technique and strength through regular or modified push-ups and introduce fist push-ups gradually, especially if they have any wrist, hand, finger, or shoulder issues.

article_title: Pune Rains News Live Updates: Minor landslide hits Chandanapuri Ghat, no casualties
sub_title: Mumbai-Pune Rains News Today Live Updates: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has declared a holiday for all government, private, and municipal schools and colleges in Mumbai today
article_content: Incessant rain has significantly raised the water level at Sangam, where the Mula and Mutha rivers converge, in Pune on Tuesday. Around 3.30 pm a minor landslide occurred on the Pune-bound carriageway of the Pune–Mumbai Expressway near Lonavala, resulting in rocks and debris falling onto the roadway. As a precautionary measure, traffic is being regulated through a single lane while debris clearance is being carried out by IRB. The carriageway is expected to be fully cleared and normal traffic movement restored within one hour. A minor landslide occurred on Monday afternoon on NH-60 at Chandanapuri Ghat on the Nashik to Pune carriageway. The debris was immediately cleared with the help of earthmovers, and traffic was restored without delay. There has been no loss of life or damage to property. Traffic on the highway is presently smooth and normal. Highway Police are continuously patrolling the area and monitoring the situation. Mumbai-Pune train services remained affected on Tuesday following landslides between Thakurvadi Cabin and Monkey Hill Cabin in the Lonavala-Karjat ghat section, which caused extensive damage to infrastructure. According to the latest Central Railway update, 14 trains were cancelled, five were diverted, three were short-terminated, three were short-originated, and one was rescheduled due to the disruption. Among the cancelled trains were the Pune-CSMT Deccan Express, CSMT-Pune Deccan Queen, Pune-CSMT Pragati Express, Pune-CSMT Intercity Express, Pune-CSMT Indrayani Express, CSMT-Pune Sinhagad Express, and the Pune-Solapur Intercity Express. (PTI) Heavy rainfall caused the Alandi River to overflow, forcing authorities to close all four bridges to vehicular traffic as a precautionary measure. VIDEO | Pune, Maharashtra: Alandi River overflows amid heavy rainfall in the region. All four bridges closed for traffic. #punerains #punenews #monsoon (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/n147TvrpG7 ) pic.twitter.com/EbYHLOeZKG Lonavala has experienced exceptional rainfall, with the India Meteorological Department recording 670 mm in a 24-hour period, an occurrence statistically estimated to happen once every millennium. Our habit is to rob our own motherland, the High Court said as it pointed to encroachment of footpaths, rendering them inaccessible for pedestrians. Citizens should stop blaming the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) alone for monsoon water-logging, a bench of acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad said, noting that encroachments and clogged drains are "our own creation" and flooding is obvious during monsoon. PTI El Nino, the recurrent weather pattern that drives up global temperatures, and climate change cannot be viewed independently as one is delaying the rains and the other intensifying them, according to climate experts. A rapidly strengthening El Nino in the Pacific delayed the onset of the monsoon and kept rainfall subdued through June, leaving India with a 40 per cent rainfall deficit by the end of the month. Yet, within days, the scenario changed dramatically. As the monsoon entered an active phase by the end of June, Mumbai and large parts of India's West Coast were battered by exceptionally intense rainfall. Experts say the new reality that climate change is fundamentally altering the behaviour of the Indian monsoon. "Monsoon is presently in an active phase, with several weather systems prevailing across the country. There was a depression over Odisha and a cyclonic circulation over Maharashtra, keeping the western and eastern arms of monsoon active," said Mahesh Palawat, Vice President - Meteorology and Climate Change, Skymet Weather. "Along with this, continuous moisture feed from the Arabian Sea led to continuous regeneration of clouds over Maharashtra in the last three-four days, leading to heavy rainfall," Palawat said. Raghu Murtugudde, Emeritus Professor, University of Maryland and retired professor, IIT-Mumbai, explained that Mumbai saw delayed onset of monsoon which is partly explainable by El Nino. Mumbai and its trees According to the BMC’s 2011 tree census, Mumbai had nearly 29.75 lakh trees. However, the actual number is likely to be lower today, as a significant portion of the city’s green cover has been lost over the past decade to infrastructure projects. Repeated tree collapses during successive monsoons have also contributed to the decline. Besides parks and open spaces, a large number of trees line Mumbai’s roads. Most are indigenous species such as neem, peepal, banyan and gulmohar. Many of these mature trees grow over 20 metres tall and have expansive canopies that provide much-needed shade and ecological benefits. These roadside trees are planted in square-shaped soil pits, commonly known as tree basins. However, experts have long criticised the maintenance of these basins, pointing out that many have been encroached upon by cement and concrete during road widening, road concretisation, utility trenching, fibre-optic cable laying and stormwater drain projects. According to orthopaedic specialist Dr Mrinal Prakash, knuckle push-ups help build upper-body strength, improve wrist and forearm stability, grip strength, muscular endurance, and body control because the exercise is performed on a much smaller base of support than regular push-ups. While Khali’s ability to perform them demonstrates impressive strength, coordination, and control, the exercise is significantly more demanding on the knuckles, wrists, shoulders, and core. article_title: Pune Rains News Live Updates: Minor landslide hits Chandanapuri Ghat, no casualties
sub_title: Mumbai-Pune Rains News Today Live Updates: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has declared a holiday for all government, private, and municipal schools and colleges in Mumbai today
article_content: Incessant rain has significantly raised the water level at Sangam, where the Mula and Mutha rivers converge, in Pune on Tuesday. Around 3.30 pm a minor landslide occurred on the Pune-bound carriageway of the Pune–Mumbai Expressway near Lonavala, resulting in rocks and debris falling onto the roadway. As a precautionary measure, traffic is being regulated through a single lane while debris clearance is being carried out by IRB. The carriageway is expected to be fully cleared and normal traffic movement restored within one hour. A minor landslide occurred on Monday afternoon on NH-60 at Chandanapuri Ghat on the Nashik to Pune carriageway. The debris was immediately cleared with the help of earthmovers, and traffic was restored without delay. There has been no loss of life or damage to property. Traffic on the highway is presently smooth and normal. Highway Police are continuously patrolling the area and monitoring the situation. Mumbai-Pune train services remained affected on Tuesday following landslides between Thakurvadi Cabin and Monkey Hill Cabin in the Lonavala-Karjat ghat section, which caused extensive damage to infrastructure. According to the latest Central Railway update, 14 trains were cancelled, five were diverted, three were short-terminated, three were short-originated, and one was rescheduled due to the disruption. Among the cancelled trains were the Pune-CSMT Deccan Express, CSMT-Pune Deccan Queen, Pune-CSMT Pragati Express, Pune-CSMT Intercity Express, Pune-CSMT Indrayani Express, CSMT-Pune Sinhagad Express, and the Pune-Solapur Intercity Express. (PTI) Heavy rainfall caused the Alandi River to overflow, forcing authorities to close all four bridges to vehicular traffic as a precautionary measure. VIDEO | Pune, Maharashtra: Alandi River overflows amid heavy rainfall in the region. All four bridges closed for traffic. #punerains #punenews #monsoon (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/n147TvrpG7 ) pic.twitter.com/EbYHLOeZKG Lonavala has experienced exceptional rainfall, with the India Meteorological Department recording 670 mm in a 24-hour period, an occurrence statistically estimated to happen once every millennium. The Ghat regions of Maharashtra, which include Lonavala, remain under a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall, though conditions are anticipated to ease as the alert is downgraded to orange by Wednesday. Due to heavy rainfall and weather alerts issued by the India Meteorological Department, Pune schools remained closed on July 6 and 7, 2026, leading several institutions to implement different strategies to compensate for the lost instructional time. While schools such as The Bishop’s School, St. Mary’s School, and The Kalyani School are conducting online classes or providing home worksheets to ensure continuity, other institutions like Sanskriti School plan to make up for the missed days by utilising a compensatory Saturday. Alternatively, Jnana Prabodhini school has declared a complete holiday for students and tasked teachers with completing professional development courses via the Diksha platform, while some schools have also chosen to postpone unit tests until in-person classes resume. The Godavari River crossed the danger level in Nashik following incessant heavy rainfall on Tuesday (Jul 7), prompting authorities to remain on high alert. VIDEO | Water level crossed the danger mark in the Godavari river due to continuous heavy rainfall in Maharashtra's Nashik. Authorities on high alert. #nashik pic.twitter.com/32oy6NVCm0 The water level of the Godavari River in Nashik rose following torrential rainfall, prompting authorities to deploy security personnel at the Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga temple to ensure the safety of devotees and visitors. VIDEO | Maharashtra: Water level of Godavari River in Nashik rises following torrential rains; security personnel deployed for safety of visitors at the Triambakeshwar Jyotirling temple. (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/n147TvrpG7 ) pic.twitter.com/xpiHRElvHI Due to heavy rain and the Palkhi procession, operations at the Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) have been affected. Applicants who missed their driving test at the Institute of Driving and Traffic Research (IDTR) on July 6 have been asked to reschedule and appear for the test at their convenience within the next 10 days. Those who could not attend their learner’s licence test on Monday have been told to book a fresh appointment. Pimpri-Chinchwad RTO’s Alandi Road office will suspend vehicle inspections and driving licence testing on July 9 due to the Palkhi processions of Sant Dnyaneshwar Maharaj and Sant Tukaram Maharaj. Applicants with appointments for vehicle inspection or driving licence tests scheduled on July 9 can appear for their tests on any working day between July 10 and July 20. A day after damage to the retaining structure at the Missing Link and heavy water flow disrupted traffic on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, vehicular movement remained largely normal on Tuesday, albeit slower than usual. The Highway Police and the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) have advised motorists to avoid non-essential travel as intermittent rain continues. MSRDC and the construction company cleared the debris from the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway of the Missing Link shortly after 10 pm on Monday. Traffic was restored on two lanes after the stretch was inspected and certified safe by MSRDC, the road safety engineer and the contractor. ANI A hearing on a plea by the Mumbai civic body turned into a blunt assessment of the civic sense of citizens on Tuesday, with the Bombay High Court flagging the people's "uncanny knack" for land grab and dumping of waste in drains, which it said causes water-logging in monsoon. Our habit is to rob our own motherland, the High Court said as it pointed to encroachment of footpaths, rendering them inaccessible for pedestrians. Citizens should stop blaming the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) alone for monsoon water-logging, a bench of acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad said, noting that encroachments and clogged drains are "our own creation" and flooding is obvious during monsoon. "We have an uncanny knack for grabbing lands. We put all the dirt and material inside, and we block the gutters. One small spell of rain blocks the roads in Mumbai. It's our own creation," the bench said. PTI El Nino, the recurrent weather pattern that drives up global temperatures, and climate change cannot be viewed independently as one is delaying the rains and the other intensifying them, according to climate experts. A rapidly strengthening El Nino in the Pacific delayed the onset of the monsoon and kept rainfall subdued through June, leaving India with a 40 per cent rainfall deficit by the end of the month. Yet, within days, the scenario changed dramatically. As the monsoon entered an active phase by the end of June, Mumbai and large parts of India's West Coast were battered by exceptionally intense rainfall. Experts say the new reality that climate change is fundamentally altering the behaviour of the Indian monsoon. "Monsoon is presently in an active phase, with several weather systems prevailing across the country. There was a depression over Odisha and a cyclonic circulation over Maharashtra, keeping the western and eastern arms of monsoon active," said Mahesh Palawat, Vice President - Meteorology and Climate Change, Skymet Weather. "Along with this, continuous moisture feed from the Arabian Sea led to continuous regeneration of clouds over Maharashtra in the last three-four days, leading to heavy rainfall," Palawat said. Raghu Murtugudde, Emeritus Professor, University of Maryland and retired professor, IIT-Mumbai, explained that Mumbai saw delayed onset of monsoon which is partly explainable by El Nino. PTI The sowing area across eight districts of the Marathwada region in Maharashtra shrank by 17.87 lakh hectares compared to the corresponding period last year due to the delayed onset of monsoon, officials said on Tuesday. The overall sowing percentage in the region comprising Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Jalna, Beed, Parbhani, Nanded, Hingoli, Dharashiv and Latur districts is around 58 per cent. The average land under cultivation in the last five years was 49.72 lakh hectares. In 2025, sowing took place on 42.42 lakh hectares. However, the area under cultivation shrank to 24.55 lakh hectares as of now, according to a report from the agriculture department. Waterlogging in Virar has largely subsided, though a few pockets remain flooded following Monday's heavy showers. Chief Public Relations Officer of Central Railway Swapnil Nila had earlier said the ballast washout was reported at kilometre 109/10-11 between Lowjee and Dolavli stations, forcing the suspension of train services on the section. Suburban services on all four Central Railway corridors, namely the Main Line, Harbour Line, Trans-Harbour Line and Belapur-Uran Line were operating normally with some delays. Brief disruptions were witnessed after a plastic sheet got entangled with an overhead equipment (OHE) portal near Bhandup station on the Main Line around 1.30 pm and the branch of a tree fell near GTB station on the Harbour Line, officials said. PTI Debris from the landslide on the Missing Link of the Mumbai Pune Expressway at the exit on Tunnel 2 has been cleared, MSRDC officials said. Rain-related incidents have already claimed 10 lives in Mumbai. Behind the death count are several tree-fall incidents that crushed vehicles and claimed lives. The collapse of a makeshift chawl in Mankhurd last night left six people, including five children, dead. Earlier on Sunday, a 63-year-old man died after a tree branch fell on him in Kurla. An 18-year-old boy died after a tree branch fell on him in Aarey on Saturday night. Earlier this week, an 11-year-old boy died after a tree crushed a school bus in Chembur on June 30, and a 55-year-old man died after falling into an open manhole in Sakinaka on July 2. Amid the rain fury, Maharashtra Congress president Harshvardhan Sapkal targeted the state government, alleging that the 12 rain-related deaths reported in the Mumbai region were the result of "administrative failure" and a "man-made disaster", not a natural calamity. Ishika Gupta reports Between July 1 and July 5, Mumbai reported 559 tree-fall incidents, including 203 cases in the last 24 hours alone. In less than a week, three people—including an 11-year-old boy—lost their lives, while several others were injured in multiple tree-fall incidents across the city. While tree collapses are a recurring feature of the monsoon season, this year’s surge has been unprecedented, raising serious concerns over public safety. According to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s (BMC) data, 687 tree-fall incidents were reported in 2023, 653 in 2024 and 855 in 2025. The spike in such incidents has also put the spotlight on the BMC’s ambitious Rs 17,000-crore road concreting project. Notably, two of the three fatal tree-collapse incidents occurred along roads that had recently been concretised, prompting fresh questions over whether the project may have compromised the stability of roadside trees. Mumbai and its trees According to the BMC’s 2011 tree census, Mumbai had nearly 29.75 lakh trees. However, the actual number is likely to be lower today, as a significant portion of the city’s green cover has been lost over the past decade to infrastructure projects. Repeated tree collapses during successive monsoons have also contributed to the decline. Besides parks and open spaces, a large number of trees line Mumbai’s roads. Most are indigenous species such as neem, peepal, banyan and gulmohar. Many of these mature trees grow over 20 metres tall and have expansive canopies that provide much-needed shade and ecological benefits. These roadside trees are planted in square-shaped soil pits, commonly known as tree basins. However, experts have long criticised the maintenance of these basins, pointing out that many have been encroached upon by cement and concrete during road widening, road concretisation, utility trenching, fibre-optic cable laying and stormwater drain projects. Developers, contractors, architects, project managers and site engineers have been directed to secure scaffolding, cranes, tin sheets, loose materials and other temporary structures to prevent accidents. sub_title: Mumbai Rains Weather Forecast Today Live News Updates: Mumbai schools and colleges remain closed on Tuesday as the IMD issues an orange alert for heavy rain and gusty winds. Check the latest weather update and disruptions.
article_content: Maharashtra Chief Minister's Office (CMO) on Tuesday asked farmers to plan agricultural activities in accordance with the weather situation as a significant decrease in rainfall is expected in parts of the state from July 8. While parts of Maharashtra faced heavy rainfall, the state's Agriculture Department urged the farmers in areas with less than satisfactory rainfall not to rush into sowing until sufficient moisture is created in the soil. In a statement on X, the CMO stated, "Although there was heavy rainfall in Mumbai and Western Maharashtra at the beginning of July, rainfall across various parts of the state so far has been below average. Particularly, the amount of rainfall is low in Khandesh (Dhule and Nandurbar), Central Maharashtra (Ahilyanagar and Solapur), parts of Western Vidarbha, and some areas of Marathwada." ANI A hearing on a plea by the Mumbai civic body turned into a blunt assessment of the civic sense of citizens on Tuesday, with the Bombay High Court flagging the people's "uncanny knack" for land grab and dumping of waste in drains, which it said causes water-logging in monsoon. Our habit is to rob our own motherland, the High Court said as it pointed to encroachment of footpaths, rendering them inaccessible for pedestrians. Citizens should stop blaming the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) alone for monsoon water-logging, a bench of acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad said, noting that encroachments and clogged drains are "our own creation" and flooding is obvious during monsoon. "We have an uncanny knack for grabbing lands. We put all the dirt and material inside, and we block the gutters. One small spell of rain blocks the roads in Mumbai. It's our own creation," the bench said. PTI El Nino, the recurrent weather pattern that drives up global temperatures, and climate change cannot be viewed independently as one is delaying the rains and the other intensifying them, according to climate experts. A rapidly strengthening El Nino in the Pacific delayed the onset of the monsoon and kept rainfall subdued through June, leaving India with a 40 per cent rainfall deficit by the end of the month. Yet, within days, the scenario changed dramatically. As the monsoon entered an active phase by the end of June, Mumbai and large parts of India's West Coast were battered by exceptionally intense rainfall. Experts say the new reality that climate change is fundamentally altering the behaviour of the Indian monsoon. "Monsoon is presently in an active phase, with several weather systems prevailing across the country. There was a depression over Odisha and a cyclonic circulation over Maharashtra, keeping the western and eastern arms of monsoon active," said Mahesh Palawat, Vice President - Meteorology and Climate Change, Skymet Weather. "Along with this, continuous moisture feed from the Arabian Sea led to continuous regeneration of clouds over Maharashtra in the last three-four days, leading to heavy rainfall," Palawat said. Raghu Murtugudde, Emeritus Professor, University of Maryland and retired professor, IIT-Mumbai, explained that Mumbai saw delayed onset of monsoon which is partly explainable by El Nino. PTI The sowing area across eight districts of the Marathwada region in Maharashtra shrank by 17.87 lakh hectares compared to the corresponding period last year due to the delayed onset of monsoon, officials said on Tuesday. The overall sowing percentage in the region comprising Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Jalna, Beed, Parbhani, Nanded, Hingoli, Dharashiv and Latur districts is around 58 per cent. The average land under cultivation in the last five years was 49.72 lakh hectares. In 2025, sowing took place on 42.42 lakh hectares. However, the area under cultivation shrank to 24.55 lakh hectares as of now, according to a report from the agriculture department. PTI Around 3.30 pm a minor landslide occurred on the Pune-bound carriageway of the Pune–Mumbai Expressway near Lonavala, resulting in rocks and debris falling onto the roadway. As a precautionary measure, traffic is being regulated through a single lane while debris clearance is being carried out by IRB. The carriageway is expected to be fully cleared and normal traffic movement restored within one hour. Two minor boys drowned, while two women suffered injuries as cement sheets collapsed at a garden in Mumbai during heavy rains and winds during the last 24 hours, officials said on Tuesday. The two boys, aged 17 and 14, drowned in flood waters in Malad and Govandi areas on Monday evening. Meanwhile, the two women were injured after cement sheets from an adjoining structure collapsed while they were practising yoga at a private garden in the Lokhandwala area in Andheri. They were admitted to the hospital and reported to be in stable condition, the BMC said. Waterlogging in Virar has largely subsided, though a few pockets remain flooded following Monday's heavy showers. (Express Photos by Akash Patil) s Bombay High Court recently observed that Mumbai's frequent flooding is a man-made issue caused by illegal land grabbing, the obstruction of drainage systems, and the unauthorized use of footpaths for commercial and parking purposes, rather than being solely the fault of the Municipal Corporation. During a hearing regarding road widening in Mandala village, the court criticized the public for ignoring legal standards until facing demolition notices, while also addressing the ongoing dispute over expanding a road near the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre. The BMC reported that while they have cleared encroachments for a 30-foot road, further widening to 50 feet requires the cooperation of the Union Department of Atomic Energy, which the court has now formally notified to provide a decision. Lonavala has experienced exceptional rainfall, with the India Meteorological Department recording 670 mm in a 24-hour period, an occurrence statistically estimated to happen once every millennium. The Ghat regions of Maharashtra, which include Lonavala, remain under a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall, though conditions are anticipated to ease as the alert is downgraded to orange by Wednesday. The members of Opposition, on Tuesday, demanded a discussion on the rain situation in the Maharashtra assembly, citing widespread damage and a rising death toll. Speaker Rahul Narwekar said that the adjournment notices moved by the Opposition did not meet the rules and were not admitted. However, he asked the Opposition to raise the issue via a half-an-hour discussion. Representatives from the Congress, NCP (SP), and Shiv Sena (UBT) highlighted severe disruptions in both urban and rural areas. Jayant Patil of NCP (SP) said that 12 people were killed in rain-related incidents over the last two to three days. Alleging administrative lapses, he emphasised that the Opposition wanted the government to respond to the situation. Heavy rainfall continued to lash parts of Thane city on Tuesday (Jul 7), with visuals from the Rabodi area showing intense showers as monsoon activity remained vigorous across Maharashtra. Rescue teams are on the scene after one person was rescued, while efforts continue to reach those still trapped. The building collapse in Mumbai’s Mankhurd that claimed six lives, including five minors, has once again turned the spotlight on the area’s long-standing problem of illegal and structurally unsafe housing. The Mankhurd-Shivaji Nagar belt is dotted with informal settlements, ageing chawls and unauthorised multi-storey structures, many built on low-lying land prone to flooding and prolonged waterlogging during the monsoon. Weak soil conditions, ageing buildings and rampant unauthorised construction have made these neighbourhoods among the most vulnerable in Mumbai to monsoon-related collapses. The Karjat-Khopoli section is part of Mumbai's suburban rail network and is used by thousands of commuters every day to travel to the metropolis for work. Suburban services on all four Central Railway corridors, namely the Main Line, Harbour Line, Trans-Harbour Line and Belapur-Uran Line were operating normally with some delays. Brief disruptions were witnessed after a plastic sheet got entangled with an overhead equipment (OHE) portal near Bhandup station on the Main Line around 1.30 pm and the branch of a tree fell near GTB station on the Harbour Line, officials said. Meanwhile, train services on the Karjat-Lonavala ghat section continue to remain suspended due to multiple landslides triggered by heavy rain, officials added. PTI Debris from the landslide on the Missing Link of the Mumbai Pune Expressway at the exit on Tunnel 2 has been cleared, MSRDC officials said. Rain-related incidents have already claimed 10 lives in Mumbai. Behind the death count are several tree-fall incidents that crushed vehicles and claimed lives. The collapse of a makeshift chawl in Mankhurd last night left six people, including five children, dead. Earlier on Sunday, a 63-year-old man died after a tree branch fell on him in Kurla. An 18-year-old boy died after a tree branch fell on him in Aarey on Saturday night. Earlier this week, an 11-year-old boy died after a tree crushed a school bus in Chembur on June 30, and a 55-year-old man died after falling into an open manhole in Sakinaka on July 2. Amid the rain fury, Maharashtra Congress president Harshvardhan Sapkal targeted the state government, alleging that the 12 rain-related deaths reported in the Mumbai region were the result of "administrative failure" and a "man-made disaster", not a natural calamity. Sapkal labelled Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis a "disaster man" rather than an "infra man", accusing the BJP-led Mahayuti government of being unprepared for the monsoon. "The 12 deaths reported in the Mumbai region amid heavy rains were the result of administrative failure and a man-made disaster, not a natural calamity," he alleged. He further criticised the Rs 7,181-crore "Missing Link", alleging that the project was marred by corruption and structural deficiencies, claiming it had to be closed just two months after its inauguration. Earlier in the day, the Pune-Mumbai Expressway had been closed between the Connecting Link and Missing Link sections after a concrete pillar fell on the carriageway amid heavy rains. Sapkal claimed that experts had raised 13 specific objections - ranging from tunnel safety to geological stability near the Lonavala dam - during the previous Congress-NCP government's tenure, but the current regime ignored these concerns to rush the project for inauguration, compromising both public safety and taxpayer funds. Labelling Fadnavis a "disaster man and not infra man", he demanded that a case of culpable homicide be registered against the chief minister. PTI Five incoming flights diverted from Mumbai to other airports till 3:30pm due to heavy rains in metropolis, officials told PTI. Another tree-falling incident has been reported in Mumbai. Ishika Gupta reports Between July 1 and July 5, Mumbai reported 559 tree-fall incidents, including 203 cases in the last 24 hours alone. In less than a week, three people—including an 11-year-old boy—lost their lives, while several others were injured in multiple tree-fall incidents across the city. While tree collapses are a recurring feature of the monsoon season, this year’s surge has been unprecedented, raising serious concerns over public safety. According to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s (BMC) data, 687 tree-fall incidents were reported in 2023, 653 in 2024 and 855 in 2025. The spike in such incidents has also put the spotlight on the BMC’s ambitious Rs 17,000-crore road concreting project. Notably, two of the three fatal tree-collapse incidents occurred along roads that had recently been concretised, prompting fresh questions over whether the project may have compromised the stability of roadside trees. Mumbai and its trees According to the BMC’s 2011 tree census, Mumbai had nearly 29.75 lakh trees. However, the actual number is likely to be lower today, as a significant portion of the city’s green cover has been lost over the past decade to infrastructure projects. Repeated tree collapses during successive monsoons have also contributed to the decline. Besides parks and open spaces, a large number of trees line Mumbai’s roads. Most are indigenous species such as neem, peepal, banyan and gulmohar. Many of these mature trees grow over 20 metres tall and have expansive canopies that provide much-needed shade and ecological benefits. These roadside trees are planted in square-shaped soil pits, commonly known as tree basins. However, experts have long criticised the maintenance of these basins, pointing out that many have been encroached upon by cement and concrete during road widening, road concretisation, utility trenching, fibre-optic cable laying and stormwater drain projects. Airlines, including IndiGo and Akasa Air, also issued travel advisories, while normal flight operations resumed on Monday. Developers, contractors, architects, project managers and site engineers have been directed to secure scaffolding, cranes, tin sheets, loose materials and other temporary structures to prevent accidents. Stressing that the safety of workers, nearby residents and the public is paramount, the BMC warned that compliance with the advisory is mandatory until weather conditions improve. The victims included a woman and her children, along with children from a nearby home who had come over to stay. A 24-year-old passerby was seriously injured but is now reported to be stable. Rescue teams from the fire department and the NDRF completed operations early Monday, confirming no one else was trapped. article_content: Incessant rain has significantly raised the water level at Sangam, where the Mula and Mutha rivers converge, in Pune on Tuesday. Around 3.30 pm a minor landslide occurred on the Pune-bound carriageway of the Pune–Mumbai Expressway near Lonavala, resulting in rocks and debris falling onto the roadway. As a precautionary measure, traffic is being regulated through a single lane while debris clearance is being carried out by IRB. The carriageway is expected to be fully cleared and normal traffic movement restored within one hour. A minor landslide occurred on Monday afternoon on NH-60 at Chandanapuri Ghat on the Nashik to Pune carriageway. The debris was immediately cleared with the help of earthmovers, and traffic was restored without delay. There has been no loss of life or damage to property. Traffic on the highway is presently smooth and normal. Highway Police are continuously patrolling the area and monitoring the situation. Mumbai-Pune train services remained affected on Tuesday following landslides between Thakurvadi Cabin and Monkey Hill Cabin in the Lonavala-Karjat ghat section, which caused extensive damage to infrastructure. According to the latest Central Railway update, 14 trains were cancelled, five were diverted, three were short-terminated, three were short-originated, and one was rescheduled due to the disruption. Among the cancelled trains were the Pune-CSMT Deccan Express, CSMT-Pune Deccan Queen, Pune-CSMT Pragati Express, Pune-CSMT Intercity Express, Pune-CSMT Indrayani Express, CSMT-Pune Sinhagad Express, and the Pune-Solapur Intercity Express. The Ghat regions of Maharashtra, which include Lonavala, remain under a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall, though conditions are anticipated to ease as the alert is downgraded to orange by Wednesday. While schools such as The Bishop’s School, St. Mary’s School, and The Kalyani School are conducting online classes or providing home worksheets to ensure continuity, other institutions like Sanskriti School plan to make up for the missed days by utilising a compensatory Saturday. A day after damage to the retaining structure at the Missing Link and heavy water flow disrupted traffic on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, vehicular movement remained largely normal on Tuesday, albeit slower than usual. The Highway Police and the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) have advised motorists to avoid non-essential travel as intermittent rain continues. MSRDC and the construction company cleared the debris from the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway of the Missing Link shortly after 10 pm on Monday. Traffic was restored on two lanes after the stretch was inspected and certified safe by MSRDC, the road safety engineer and the contractor. The remaining two lanes have been kept closed due to intermittent water flow from the adjoining hillside. Over the past 48 hours, the Pune district has experienced severe weather conditions, resulting in 22 landslides, four deaths, one missing person, and over 20 injuries. District Collector Jitendra Dudi reported that extensive relief efforts, coordinated by agencies including the NDRF and local authorities, have successfully relocated over 270 citizens and rescued 30 people from a stranded bus. The heavy rainfall has caused significant infrastructure disruption, leading to the closure of nine rural roads, the Pune-Mumbai Expressway's Missing Link, and the Varandha Ghat road until August 31. While officials continue to monitor rising water levels at the Khadakwasla Dam and have temporarily restricted tourist access to forts near Lonavala, they are carefully balancing reservoir management with flood prevention measures during this El Niño year. Heavy rainfall in Pune on Monday (Jul 6), caused widespread disruption to both air and rail transport. At Pune Airport, flight operations were impacted by cancellations, diversions, and delays, prompting airlines to advise passengers to check their flight status and allow extra time for travel. Simultaneously, a major landslide in the Lonavala-Karjat section severely affected rail services, resulting in the cancellation of 26 trains, the diversion of 47 others, and various short-terminations and rescheduling, with restoration work currently underway involving hundreds of laborers. The water level of the Mula-Mutha river rises following heavy rainfall, as authorities issue a high alert over the rising water level. With the reservoir reaching 62 percent capacity and expected to exceed 80 percent soon, authorities have advised citizens to stay out of the riverbed and relocate any vehicles or animals immediately. While recent heavy rains have significantly improved water storage levels—doubling the supply to 7 TMC from 3 TMC—civic bodies are closely monitoring the situation to determine if current water cuts in the city can be adjusted. Barely nine weeks after its inauguration, the Rs 6,695-crore Missing Link on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway suffered its first major monsoon disruption after a landslide damaged a retaining structure near Tunnel 2, forcing the closure of the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway. While traffic on the Mumbai-to-Pune side resumed from around 10 am, Mumbai-bound vehicles continued to be diverted via the old Mumbai-Pune Highway and the ghat section as repair work and safety inspections continued. The Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) attributed the incident to exceptionally heavy rainfall, calling it an "act of God" rather than a construction flaw. Officials said the tunnel remained structurally safe, with damage confined to the retaining structure and the tunnel's external false frame. The agency said rockfall protection systems vetted by IIT Bombay remained intact and had prevented a more serious accident, while a fresh geological assessment will be carried out after the monsoon. The Rs 6,695-crore Mumbai-Pune Expressway Missing Link, inaugurated on May 1 as a solution to the expressway's busiest bottleneck, was partially shut on Monday after a rain-triggered landslide damaged a retaining structure near Tunnel 2. The Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway remains closed, forcing traffic onto the old Mumbai-Pune Highway, while the Mumbai-to-Pune carriageway has reopened in phases. article_title: Pune Rains News Live Updates: Minor landslide hits Chandanapuri Ghat, no casualties
sub_title: Mumbai-Pune Rains News Today Live Updates: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has declared a holiday for all government, private, and municipal schools and colleges in Mumbai today
article_content: Incessant rain has significantly raised the water level at Sangam, where the Mula and Mutha rivers converge, in Pune on Tuesday. Around 3.30 pm a minor landslide occurred on the Pune-bound carriageway of the Pune–Mumbai Expressway near Lonavala, resulting in rocks and debris falling onto the roadway. As a precautionary measure, traffic is being regulated through a single lane while debris clearance is being carried out by IRB. The carriageway is expected to be fully cleared and normal traffic movement restored within one hour. A minor landslide occurred on Monday afternoon on NH-60 at Chandanapuri Ghat on the Nashik to Pune carriageway. The debris was immediately cleared with the help of earthmovers, and traffic was restored without delay. There has been no loss of life or damage to property. Traffic on the highway is presently smooth and normal. Highway Police are continuously patrolling the area and monitoring the situation. Mumbai-Pune train services remained affected on Tuesday following landslides between Thakurvadi Cabin and Monkey Hill Cabin in the Lonavala-Karjat ghat section, which caused extensive damage to infrastructure. According to the latest Central Railway update, 14 trains were cancelled, five were diverted, three were short-terminated, three were short-originated, and one was rescheduled due to the disruption. Among the cancelled trains were the Pune-CSMT Deccan Express, CSMT-Pune Deccan Queen, Pune-CSMT Pragati Express, Pune-CSMT Intercity Express, Pune-CSMT Indrayani Express, CSMT-Pune Sinhagad Express, and the Pune-Solapur Intercity Express. (PTI) Heavy rainfall caused the Alandi River to overflow, forcing authorities to close all four bridges to vehicular traffic as a precautionary measure. VIDEO | Pune, Maharashtra: Alandi River overflows amid heavy rainfall in the region. All four bridges closed for traffic. #punerains #punenews #monsoon (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/n147TvrpG7 ) pic.twitter.com/EbYHLOeZKG Lonavala has experienced exceptional rainfall, with the India Meteorological Department recording 670 mm in a 24-hour period, an occurrence statistically estimated to happen once every millennium. The Ghat regions of Maharashtra, which include Lonavala, remain under a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall, though conditions are anticipated to ease as the alert is downgraded to orange by Wednesday. Due to heavy rainfall and weather alerts issued by the India Meteorological Department, Pune schools remained closed on July 6 and 7, 2026, leading several institutions to implement different strategies to compensate for the lost instructional time. While schools such as The Bishop’s School, St. Mary’s School, and The Kalyani School are conducting online classes or providing home worksheets to ensure continuity, other institutions like Sanskriti School plan to make up for the missed days by utilising a compensatory Saturday. Alternatively, Jnana Prabodhini school has declared a complete holiday for students and tasked teachers with completing professional development courses via the Diksha platform, while some schools have also chosen to postpone unit tests until in-person classes resume. The Godavari River crossed the danger level in Nashik following incessant heavy rainfall on Tuesday (Jul 7), prompting authorities to remain on high alert. VIDEO | Water level crossed the danger mark in the Godavari river due to continuous heavy rainfall in Maharashtra's Nashik. Authorities on high alert. #nashik pic.twitter.com/32oy6NVCm0 The water level of the Godavari River in Nashik rose following torrential rainfall, prompting authorities to deploy security personnel at the Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga temple to ensure the safety of devotees and visitors. VIDEO | Maharashtra: Water level of Godavari River in Nashik rises following torrential rains; security personnel deployed for safety of visitors at the Triambakeshwar Jyotirling temple. (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/n147TvrpG7 ) pic.twitter.com/xpiHRElvHI Due to heavy rain and the Palkhi procession, operations at the Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) have been affected. Applicants who missed their driving test at the Institute of Driving and Traffic Research (IDTR) on July 6 have been asked to reschedule and appear for the test at their convenience within the next 10 days. Those who could not attend their learner’s licence test on Monday have been told to book a fresh appointment. Pimpri-Chinchwad RTO’s Alandi Road office will suspend vehicle inspections and driving licence testing on July 9 due to the Palkhi processions of Sant Dnyaneshwar Maharaj and Sant Tukaram Maharaj. Applicants with appointments for vehicle inspection or driving licence tests scheduled on July 9 can appear for their tests on any working day between July 10 and July 20. A day after damage to the retaining structure at the Missing Link and heavy water flow disrupted traffic on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, vehicular movement remained largely normal on Tuesday, albeit slower than usual. The Highway Police and the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) have advised motorists to avoid non-essential travel as intermittent rain continues. MSRDC and the construction company cleared the debris from the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway of the Missing Link shortly after 10 pm on Monday. Traffic was restored on two lanes after the stretch was inspected and certified safe by MSRDC, the road safety engineer and the contractor. The remaining two lanes have been kept closed due to intermittent water flow from the adjoining hillside. Over the past 48 hours, the Pune district has experienced severe weather conditions, resulting in 22 landslides, four deaths, one missing person, and over 20 injuries. District Collector Jitendra Dudi reported that extensive relief efforts, coordinated by agencies including the NDRF and local authorities, have successfully relocated over 270 citizens and rescued 30 people from a stranded bus. The heavy rainfall has caused significant infrastructure disruption, leading to the closure of nine rural roads, the Pune-Mumbai Expressway's Missing Link, and the Varandha Ghat road until August 31. While officials continue to monitor rising water levels at the Khadakwasla Dam and have temporarily restricted tourist access to forts near Lonavala, they are carefully balancing reservoir management with flood prevention measures during this El Niño year. Heavy rainfall in Pune on Monday (Jul 6), caused widespread disruption to both air and rail transport. At Pune Airport, flight operations were impacted by cancellations, diversions, and delays, prompting airlines to advise passengers to check their flight status and allow extra time for travel. Simultaneously, a major landslide in the Lonavala-Karjat section severely affected rail services, resulting in the cancellation of 26 trains, the diversion of 47 others, and various short-terminations and rescheduling, with restoration work currently underway involving hundreds of laborers. The water level of the Mula-Mutha river rises following heavy rainfall, as authorities issue a high alert over the rising water level. Due to heavy rainfall in the Khadakwasla Dam catchment area, the Pune district administration has issued an alert to residents in low-lying areas along the Mutha river, warning that water may be released from the dam's spillway at any time. With the reservoir reaching 62 percent capacity and expected to exceed 80 percent soon, authorities have advised citizens to stay out of the riverbed and relocate any vehicles or animals immediately. While recent heavy rains have significantly improved water storage levels—doubling the supply to 7 TMC from 3 TMC—civic bodies are closely monitoring the situation to determine if current water cuts in the city can be adjusted. Traffic on the Pune–Mumbai corridor of the Missing Link resumed after remaining disrupted for more than 18 hours, bringing relief to thousands of commuters stranded or affected by the prolonged closure. Authorities restored vehicular movement after ensuring the route was safe for travel following adverse weather conditions. Even as traffic has resumed, officials have urged commuters to avoid non-essential travel in view of the continuing heavy monsoon. The commuters are advised to strictly adhere to traffic advisories issued by the authorities as the rainfall may continue to impact traffic movement in the region. 🚨 IMPORTANT UPDATE ✅ Traffic has resumed on the Pune–Mumbai Connecting Link Road. Vehicular movement has been restored after completion of extensive safety operations. Despite relentless monsoon conditions, including heavy rainfall, strong winds and low visibility, MSRDC… pic.twitter.com/LCRirbWao0 The Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) on Monday evacuated residents from low-lying and riverside areas after continuous rainfall raised the risk of flooding. Residents from Ambedkar Colony, Bhatnagar and River Road were shifted to relief shelters, while evacuations were also underway in Fugewadi and Kasarwadi. Emergency teams have been deployed across the city, with JCBs, water pumps and other machinery pressed into service to tackle waterlogging in Chikhli and other affected areas. Fire department personnel also rescued a pregnant woman trapped in floodwaters at Kiwale Gaothan. PCMC Commissioner Vijay Suryavanshi urged residents to avoid unnecessary travel, stay away from rivers and flood-affected areas, and follow official advisories. NCP working president and Baramati MP Supriya Sule on Monday urged the Maharashtra government to allow IT employees to work from home as incessant rain disrupted normal life across Mumbai, Pune and surrounding areas. In a letter to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Sule requested that employees in establishments where remote work is feasible, including those in Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park at Hinjewadi, be allowed to work from home. Her appeal came after the Forum for IT Employees and the Pimpri Chinchwad Cooperative Housing Society Federation sought temporary WFH arrangements, citing waterlogged roads, traffic snarls and safety concerns. Sule also urged residents, particularly those living near rivers, to remain vigilant and follow official advisories. Read the full report at The Indian Express here. While traffic on the Mumbai-to-Pune side resumed from around 10 am, Mumbai-bound vehicles continued to be diverted via the old Mumbai-Pune Highway and the ghat section as repair work and safety inspections continued. The Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) attributed the incident to exceptionally heavy rainfall, calling it an "act of God" rather than a construction flaw. Officials said the tunnel remained structurally safe, with damage confined to the retaining structure and the tunnel's external false frame. The agency said rockfall protection systems vetted by IIT Bombay remained intact and had prevented a more serious accident, while a fresh geological assessment will be carried out after the monsoon. Our habit is to rob our own motherland, the High Court said as it pointed to encroachment of footpaths, rendering them inaccessible for pedestrians. Citizens should stop blaming the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) alone for monsoon water-logging, a bench of acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad said, noting that encroachments and clogged drains are "our own creation" and flooding is obvious during monsoon. PTI El Nino, the recurrent weather pattern that drives up global temperatures, and climate change cannot be viewed independently as one is delaying the rains and the other intensifying them, according to climate experts. A rapidly strengthening El Nino in the Pacific delayed the onset of the monsoon and kept rainfall subdued through June, leaving India with a 40 per cent rainfall deficit by the end of the month. Yet, within days, the scenario changed dramatically. As the monsoon entered an active phase by the end of June, Mumbai and large parts of India's West Coast were battered by exceptionally intense rainfall. Experts say the new reality that climate change is fundamentally altering the behaviour of the Indian monsoon. "Monsoon is presently in an active phase, with several weather systems prevailing across the country. There was a depression over Odisha and a cyclonic circulation over Maharashtra, keeping the western and eastern arms of monsoon active," said Mahesh Palawat, Vice President - Meteorology and Climate Change, Skymet Weather. "Along with this, continuous moisture feed from the Arabian Sea led to continuous regeneration of clouds over Maharashtra in the last three-four days, leading to heavy rainfall," Palawat said. Raghu Murtugudde, Emeritus Professor, University of Maryland and retired professor, IIT-Mumbai, explained that Mumbai saw delayed onset of monsoon which is partly explainable by El Nino. Ishika Gupta reports Between July 1 and July 5, Mumbai reported 559 tree-fall incidents, including 203 cases in the last 24 hours alone. In less than a week, three people—including an 11-year-old boy—lost their lives, while several others were injured in multiple tree-fall incidents across the city. While tree collapses are a recurring feature of the monsoon season, this year’s surge has been unprecedented, raising serious concerns over public safety. According to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s (BMC) data, 687 tree-fall incidents were reported in 2023, 653 in 2024 and 855 in 2025. The spike in such incidents has also put the spotlight on the BMC’s ambitious Rs 17,000-crore road concreting project. Notably, two of the three fatal tree-collapse incidents occurred along roads that had recently been concretised, prompting fresh questions over whether the project may have compromised the stability of roadside trees. Mumbai and its trees According to the BMC’s 2011 tree census, Mumbai had nearly 29.75 lakh trees. However, the actual number is likely to be lower today, as a significant portion of the city’s green cover has been lost over the past decade to infrastructure projects. Repeated tree collapses during successive monsoons have also contributed to the decline. Besides parks and open spaces, a large number of trees line Mumbai’s roads. Most are indigenous species such as neem, peepal, banyan and gulmohar. Many of these mature trees grow over 20 metres tall and have expansive canopies that provide much-needed shade and ecological benefits. These roadside trees are planted in square-shaped soil pits, commonly known as tree basins. However, experts have long criticised the maintenance of these basins, pointing out that many have been encroached upon by cement and concrete during road widening, road concretisation, utility trenching, fibre-optic cable laying and stormwater drain projects. Airlines, including IndiGo and Akasa Air, also issued travel advisories, while normal flight operations resumed on Monday. The civic body has also ordered the suspension of lifting operations and work at heights wherever weather conditions pose a risk, while mandating site-wide safety inspections, continuous weather monitoring and strict use of protective gear by workers. Rescue teams from the fire department and the NDRF completed operations early Monday, confirming no one else was trapped. Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde said the illegally constructed building, allegedly being used as a godown, was stacked with goods that crashed onto the adjacent home when it gave way. article_title: Lausanne Diamond League Highlights: Neeraj Chopra ends 2nd
sub_title: Neeraj Chopra, a two-Olympic and two-time World Championships medallist, has a season best of 85.83m while Pathirage starts as the favourite with a SB of 92.62m.
article_content: Neeraj Chopra skipped his fifth throw, but returned for the final turn of the arm. And it was a throw of 82.15m while Pathirage had a no mark with his final throw! So Neeraj Chopra ends second behind Rumesh Pathirage. No mark from Neeraj Chopra with his fourth throw. But he stays in second spot behind Rumesh Pathirage. So far, besides Neeraj and Rumesh, only one thrower has managed to breach the 85m mark, Anderson Peters with 86.61m. Two more throws left for the top throwers. Can Neeraj Chopra overhaul the Sri Lankan? Another monster throw from Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage. His fourth attempt is 86.71m. For a change, he cannot better his previous best with his next throw like he did with his first three throws. Pritish Raj adds: Unreal consistency from Pathirage. His fourth attempt is 86.71m making it four in four above 85m Neeraj Chopra second behind Rumesh Pathirage after most of the nine throwers have had their three throws. Can the Indian overhaul the Sri Lankan in the final three throws? Neeraj Chopra's lead is shortlived! Rumesh Pathirage sends the spear 88.14m to take back the lead again and send Neeraj Chopra to second! Pritish Raj adds: It takes two to tango or in this case three. Pathirage has crossed Neeraj's mark with 88.14m to regain the lead again from Neeraj. Neeraj Chopra leads with a throw of 88.05m! He was unhappy with his firts attempt. But his second attempt is the kind he raises both hands heavenwards for! Pritish Raj adds: Neeraj Chopra!!! He steps up and with a season best. 88.05m for the double Olympic medallist in the second attempt and he takes the lead Pathirage has his second attempt ! And it's even bigger than his first attempt! So Rumesh Pathirage now has the two best throws today! Pathirage sends the spear 87.06 metres after a first throw of 85.99m. Czech javelin thrower Jakub Vadlejch , who won the silver medal behind Neeraj Chopra at the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games with a throw of 86.67 meters, has his first attempt and he manages a 77.32 metre throw on his first attempt Here we go! First sighting of Neeraj Chopra on the runway! And Neeraj throws 83.54 metre ! He's second behind Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage! He does not look too happy with his first attempt there! No mark from Curtis Thompson, but Anderson Peters gets on the board with a first throw of 77.96 metres. Provisionally moves to second. Pritish Raj adds: Anderson Peters enters the top three now with a throw of 84.76m in his second attempt. A pace-setting first attempt of a throw from the man to beat! Sri Lanka's Pathirage throws 85.99 metres ! Immediately sets a marker! Pritish Raj writes: Rumesh Pathirage and his big throws. The man is in incredible form this season and on this first throw at Lausanne takes the lead with 85.99m throw Here we go! Another edition of the Neeraj Chopra vs Rumesh Pathirage begins! Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Lausanne Diamond League's javelin throw event where Neeraj Chopra will be in action shortly.

Shivani Naik is a senior sports journalist and Assistant Editor at The Indian Express. She is widely considered one of the leading voices in Indian Olympic sports journalism, particularly known for her deep expertise in badminton, wrestling, and basketball.

Professional Profile
Role: Assistant Editor and Columnist at The Indian Express.

Specialization: While she covers a variety of sports, she is the primary authority on badminton for the publication. She also writes extensively about tennis, track and field, wrestling, and gymnastics.

Writing Style: Her work is characterized by "technical storytelling"—breaking down the biomechanics, tactics, and psychological grit of athletes. She often provides "long reads" that explore the personal journeys of athletes beyond the podium.

Key Topics & Recent Coverage (Late 2025)

Shivani Naik’s recent articles (as of December 2025) focus on the evolving landscape of Indian sports as athletes prepare for the 2026 Asian Games and beyond:

Indian Badminton's "Hulks": She has recently written about a new generation of Indian shuttlers characterized by power and physicality, such as Ayush Shetty and Sathish Karunakaran, marking a shift from the traditionally finesse-based Indian style.

PV Sindhu’s Resurgence: A significant portion of her late-2025 work tracks PV Sindhu’s tactical shifts under new coaching, focusing on her "sparkle" and technical tweaks to break out of career slumps.

The "Group of Death": In December 2025, she provided detailed tactical previews for Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty’s campaign in the BWF World Tour Finals.

Tactical Deep Dives: She frequently explores technical trends, such as the rise of "backhand deception" in modern badminton and the importance of court drift management in international arenas.

Legacy and History: She often revisits the careers of legends like Saina Nehwal and Syed Modi, providing historical context to current Indian successes.

Divya Goyal is a Principal Correspondent at The Indian Express, based in Ludhiana (Punjab). She is widely recognized for her human-interest storytelling and in-depth investigative reporting on social and political issues in the region.

Professional Profile

Experience: With over 13 years in journalism, she joined The Indian Express in 2012. She previously worked with Hindustan Times.

Education: A gold medalist in English Journalism from the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC), Delhi.

Core Beats: She covers a diverse range of subjects, including gender issues, education, the Sikh diaspora, heritage, and the legacy of the Partition. She has also reported on minority communities in Pakistan and Afghanistan.

Awards and Recognition

Divya has earned significant acclaim for her sensitivity toward gender and social disparities:

Laadli Media Award (2020): For her investigative report "Punjab: The Invisible Drug Addicts," which exposed the gender disparity in treating women addicts.

Laadli Media Award (2023): For a ground report on the struggles of two girls who had to ride a boat to reach their school in a border village of Punjab.

Signature Style

Divya is known for "humanizing the news." Rather than just reporting on policy, she often focuses on the individuals affected by it—such as students dealing with exam stress, farmers struggling with diversification, or families impacted by crime. Her work often bridges the gap between West (Pakistan) and East (India) Punjab, exploring shared heritage and common struggles.

article_title: Pune Rains News Live Updates: Minor landslide hits Chandanapuri Ghat, no casualties
sub_title: Mumbai-Pune Rains News Today Live Updates: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has declared a holiday for all government, private, and municipal schools and colleges in Mumbai today
article_content: Incessant rain has significantly raised the water level at Sangam, where the Mula and Mutha rivers converge, in Pune on Tuesday. Around 3.30 pm a minor landslide occurred on the Pune-bound carriageway of the Pune–Mumbai Expressway near Lonavala, resulting in rocks and debris falling onto the roadway. As a precautionary measure, traffic is being regulated through a single lane while debris clearance is being carried out by IRB. The carriageway is expected to be fully cleared and normal traffic movement restored within one hour. A minor landslide occurred on Monday afternoon on NH-60 at Chandanapuri Ghat on the Nashik to Pune carriageway. The debris was immediately cleared with the help of earthmovers, and traffic was restored without delay. There has been no loss of life or damage to property. Traffic on the highway is presently smooth and normal. Highway Police are continuously patrolling the area and monitoring the situation. Mumbai-Pune train services remained affected on Tuesday following landslides between Thakurvadi Cabin and Monkey Hill Cabin in the Lonavala-Karjat ghat section, which caused extensive damage to infrastructure. According to the latest Central Railway update, 14 trains were cancelled, five were diverted, three were short-terminated, three were short-originated, and one was rescheduled due to the disruption. Among the cancelled trains were the Pune-CSMT Deccan Express, CSMT-Pune Deccan Queen, Pune-CSMT Pragati Express, Pune-CSMT Intercity Express, Pune-CSMT Indrayani Express, CSMT-Pune Sinhagad Express, and the Pune-Solapur Intercity Express. (PTI) Heavy rainfall caused the Alandi River to overflow, forcing authorities to close all four bridges to vehicular traffic as a precautionary measure. VIDEO | Pune, Maharashtra: Alandi River overflows amid heavy rainfall in the region. All four bridges closed for traffic. #punerains #punenews #monsoon (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/n147TvrpG7 ) pic.twitter.com/EbYHLOeZKG Lonavala has experienced exceptional rainfall, with the India Meteorological Department recording 670 mm in a 24-hour period, an occurrence statistically estimated to happen once every millennium. The Ghat regions of Maharashtra, which include Lonavala, remain under a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall, though conditions are anticipated to ease as the alert is downgraded to orange by Wednesday. Due to heavy rainfall and weather alerts issued by the India Meteorological Department, Pune schools remained closed on July 6 and 7, 2026, leading several institutions to implement different strategies to compensate for the lost instructional time. While schools such as The Bishop’s School, St. Mary’s School, and The Kalyani School are conducting online classes or providing home worksheets to ensure continuity, other institutions like Sanskriti School plan to make up for the missed days by utilising a compensatory Saturday. Alternatively, Jnana Prabodhini school has declared a complete holiday for students and tasked teachers with completing professional development courses via the Diksha platform, while some schools have also chosen to postpone unit tests until in-person classes resume. The Godavari River crossed the danger level in Nashik following incessant heavy rainfall on Tuesday (Jul 7), prompting authorities to remain on high alert. VIDEO | Water level crossed the danger mark in the Godavari river due to continuous heavy rainfall in Maharashtra's Nashik. Authorities on high alert. #nashik pic.twitter.com/32oy6NVCm0 The water level of the Godavari River in Nashik rose following torrential rainfall, prompting authorities to deploy security personnel at the Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga temple to ensure the safety of devotees and visitors. VIDEO | Maharashtra: Water level of Godavari River in Nashik rises following torrential rains; security personnel deployed for safety of visitors at the Triambakeshwar Jyotirling temple. (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/n147TvrpG7 ) pic.twitter.com/xpiHRElvHI Due to heavy rain and the Palkhi procession, operations at the Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) have been affected. Applicants who missed their driving test at the Institute of Driving and Traffic Research (IDTR) on July 6 have been asked to reschedule and appear for the test at their convenience within the next 10 days. Those who could not attend their learner’s licence test on Monday have been told to book a fresh appointment. Pimpri-Chinchwad RTO’s Alandi Road office will suspend vehicle inspections and driving licence testing on July 9 due to the Palkhi processions of Sant Dnyaneshwar Maharaj and Sant Tukaram Maharaj. Applicants with appointments for vehicle inspection or driving licence tests scheduled on July 9 can appear for their tests on any working day between July 10 and July 20. A day after damage to the retaining structure at the Missing Link and heavy water flow disrupted traffic on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, vehicular movement remained largely normal on Tuesday, albeit slower than usual. The Highway Police and the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) have advised motorists to avoid non-essential travel as intermittent rain continues. MSRDC and the construction company cleared the debris from the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway of the Missing Link shortly after 10 pm on Monday. Traffic was restored on two lanes after the stretch was inspected and certified safe by MSRDC, the road safety engineer and the contractor. The remaining two lanes have been kept closed due to intermittent water flow from the adjoining hillside. Over the past 48 hours, the Pune district has experienced severe weather conditions, resulting in 22 landslides, four deaths, one missing person, and over 20 injuries. District Collector Jitendra Dudi reported that extensive relief efforts, coordinated by agencies including the NDRF and local authorities, have successfully relocated over 270 citizens and rescued 30 people from a stranded bus. The heavy rainfall has caused significant infrastructure disruption, leading to the closure of nine rural roads, the Pune-Mumbai Expressway's Missing Link, and the Varandha Ghat road until August 31. While officials continue to monitor rising water levels at the Khadakwasla Dam and have temporarily restricted tourist access to forts near Lonavala, they are carefully balancing reservoir management with flood prevention measures during this El Niño year. Heavy rainfall in Pune on Monday (Jul 6), caused widespread disruption to both air and rail transport. At Pune Airport, flight operations were impacted by cancellations, diversions, and delays, prompting airlines to advise passengers to check their flight status and allow extra time for travel. Simultaneously, a major landslide in the Lonavala-Karjat section severely affected rail services, resulting in the cancellation of 26 trains, the diversion of 47 others, and various short-terminations and rescheduling, with restoration work currently underway involving hundreds of laborers. The water level of the Mula-Mutha river rises following heavy rainfall, as authorities issue a high alert over the rising water level. Due to heavy rainfall in the Khadakwasla Dam catchment area, the Pune district administration has issued an alert to residents in low-lying areas along the Mutha river, warning that water may be released from the dam's spillway at any time. With the reservoir reaching 62 percent capacity and expected to exceed 80 percent soon, authorities have advised citizens to stay out of the riverbed and relocate any vehicles or animals immediately. While recent heavy rains have significantly improved water storage levels—doubling the supply to 7 TMC from 3 TMC—civic bodies are closely monitoring the situation to determine if current water cuts in the city can be adjusted. Traffic on the Pune–Mumbai corridor of the Missing Link resumed after remaining disrupted for more than 18 hours, bringing relief to thousands of commuters stranded or affected by the prolonged closure. Authorities restored vehicular movement after ensuring the route was safe for travel following adverse weather conditions. Even as traffic has resumed, officials have urged commuters to avoid non-essential travel in view of the continuing heavy monsoon. The commuters are advised to strictly adhere to traffic advisories issued by the authorities as the rainfall may continue to impact traffic movement in the region. 🚨 IMPORTANT UPDATE ✅ Traffic has resumed on the Pune–Mumbai Connecting Link Road. Vehicular movement has been restored after completion of extensive safety operations. Despite relentless monsoon conditions, including heavy rainfall, strong winds and low visibility, MSRDC… pic.twitter.com/LCRirbWao0 The Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) on Monday evacuated residents from low-lying and riverside areas after continuous rainfall raised the risk of flooding. Residents from Ambedkar Colony, Bhatnagar and River Road were shifted to relief shelters, while evacuations were also underway in Fugewadi and Kasarwadi. Emergency teams have been deployed across the city, with JCBs, water pumps and other machinery pressed into service to tackle waterlogging in Chikhli and other affected areas. Fire department personnel also rescued a pregnant woman trapped in floodwaters at Kiwale Gaothan. PCMC Commissioner Vijay Suryavanshi urged residents to avoid unnecessary travel, stay away from rivers and flood-affected areas, and follow official advisories. NCP working president and Baramati MP Supriya Sule on Monday urged the Maharashtra government to allow IT employees to work from home as incessant rain disrupted normal life across Mumbai, Pune and surrounding areas. In a letter to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Sule requested that employees in establishments where remote work is feasible, including those in Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park at Hinjewadi, be allowed to work from home. Her appeal came after the Forum for IT Employees and the Pimpri Chinchwad Cooperative Housing Society Federation sought temporary WFH arrangements, citing waterlogged roads, traffic snarls and safety concerns. Sule also urged residents, particularly those living near rivers, to remain vigilant and follow official advisories. Read the full report at The Indian Express here. Barely nine weeks after its inauguration, the Rs 6,695-crore Missing Link on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway suffered its first major monsoon disruption after a landslide damaged a retaining structure near Tunnel 2, forcing the closure of the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway. While traffic on the Mumbai-to-Pune side resumed from around 10 am, Mumbai-bound vehicles continued to be diverted via the old Mumbai-Pune Highway and the ghat section as repair work and safety inspections continued. The Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) attributed the incident to exceptionally heavy rainfall, calling it an "act of God" rather than a construction flaw. Officials said the tunnel remained structurally safe, with damage confined to the retaining structure and the tunnel's external false frame. The agency said rockfall protection systems vetted by IIT Bombay remained intact and had prevented a more serious accident, while a fresh geological assessment will be carried out after the monsoon. Read the full report at The Indian Express here. Hundreds of passengers were seen waiting at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) on Monday after torrential rain severely disrupted rail connectivity, leading to the cancellation and diversion of several long-distance trains on the Central Railway mainline. (Express Photo by Ganesh Shirsekar) An two storeyed old wada Dhangar Gali in Somwar peth, located in the mid city area of Pune, collapsed amid heavy rains on Monday evening. No casualties were reported in the incident, said Pune Fire Brigade officials. No casualties were reported in the incident, said Pune Fire Brigade officials | Follow Live Updates: https://t.co/87LUNIU1ll pic.twitter.com/d3RTj6KBDs The Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) has defended the newly inaugurated Mumbai-Pune Expressway Missing Link after a landslide partially shut the corridor, insisting the incident was caused by exceptionally heavy rain and not by any construction flaw. MSRDC Vice Chairman Anilkumar Gaikwad said the tunnel remained structurally safe and that only the "false frame" at the tunnel entrance was damaged after boulders rolled down from nearly 150 metres above the protected slope. Calling the incident an "act of God", officials said IIT Bombay-vetted rockfall protection systems remained intact and had prevented a more serious accident. The corporation said it would conduct a fresh geological assessment after the monsoon to examine whether additional protection measures could be installed higher up the hillside. Read the full report here at The Indian Express. The Rs 6,695-crore Mumbai-Pune Expressway Missing Link, inaugurated on May 1 as a solution to the expressway's busiest bottleneck, was partially shut on Monday after a rain-triggered landslide damaged a retaining structure near Tunnel 2. The Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway remains closed, forcing traffic onto the old Mumbai-Pune Highway, while the Mumbai-to-Pune carriageway has reopened in phases. The 13.3-km engineering project, featuring India's tallest cable-stayed bridge of its kind and one of the world's widest road tunnels, was designed to bypass the accident-prone Khandala ghat section and cut travel time by up to 30 minutes. Defending the project, the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) said the tunnel suffered no structural damage and described the landslide as an "act of God." Read the full report here at The Indian Express. Pune witnessed heavy rainfall throughout Monday, causing the water level in the Mutha river to rise significantly. The swollen river is part of the broader impact of persistent monsoon showers across the city, with authorities keeping a close watch on rivers and reservoirs. Residents have been advised to stay away from riverbanks and low-lying areas as heavy rain is expected to continue. (Express Photos By Pavan Khengre) Debris from the landslide on the Missing Link of the Mumbai-Pune Expressway at the exit on Tunnel 2 has been cleared, MSRDC officials have said. Workers while clearing the debris. (Express Photo by Narendra Vaskar) The Mutha river rose significantly on Monday following incessant rain across Pune, with people gathering on the PMC bridge near the Pune Municipal Corporation headquarters to watch the swollen river. (Express Photographs by Arul Horizon) Heavy rainfall in Pune led to a sharp rise in the Mula river's water level on Monday, with the river flowing close to the deck of Holkar Bridge in the Khadki area. The rising water levels come amid widespread rainfall across Pune district, where several rivers and reservoirs are nearing critical levels.
